#### `AccessibleRole`

What a control is, as far as assistive technology is concerned — the word a screen reader says after the name.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Default` | `0` | Let the control decide, which is what every control does unless told otherwise. |
| `StaticText` | `1` | Static text that labels something else. |
| `PushButton` | `2` | A push button. |
| `CheckButton` | `3` | A two-state check box. |
| `RadioButton` | `4` | One of a set of mutually exclusive options. |
| `Text` | `5` | An editable text field. |
| `ComboBox` | `6` | A drop-down list. |
| `List` | `7` | A list of items. |
| `ListItem` | `8` | One item of a list. |
| `Tree` | `9` | A hierarchical list. |
| `Table` | `10` | A tabular grid of cells. |
| `Slider` | `11` | A slider the user drags along a range. |
| `ProgressBar` | `12` | A progress indicator. |
| `ScrollBar` | `13` | A scroll bar. |
| `Link` | `14` | A hyperlink. |
| `Grouping` | `15` | A group of related controls, usually with a caption. |
| `PageTabList` | `16` | A set of tab pages. |
| `PageTab` | `17` | One tab page. |
| `MenuBar` | `18` | A menu bar or menu. |
| `MenuItem` | `19` | One menu entry. |
| `ToolBar` | `20` | A tool bar. |
| `Window` | `21` | A window. |
| `Pane` | `22` | A container with no meaning of its own. |
| `Graphic` | `23` | An image. |

#### `Accordion`

An Outlook-style navigation pane (§7.9): a vertical stack of `AccordionPane`s, each a themed header row — toggle glyph, optional `ImageList` icon, caption, hover/pressed feedback — over a body of ordinary child controls. Headers keep their place; the open panes share whatever height the headers leave. `ExpandMode` decides whether opening a pane closes its siblings.

Inherits `OwnerDrawnControl`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Accordion` | `Accordion()` | Creates an empty accordion. |
| `AllowUserToOrderPanes` | `bool AllowUserToOrderPanes { get; set; }` | Whether dragging a header up or down the stack reorders the sections (PRD §14). Off by default, for the reason `AllowUserToOrderItems` is: a navigation pane whose sections move when you brush past a header is worse than one that cannot be rearranged. |
| `ExpandMode` | `AccordionExpandMode ExpandMode { get; set; }` | Whether opening a pane closes the others (`Single`, the default) or panes toggle independently. Switching to `Single` while several panes are open collapses all but the selected one. |
| `Focusable` | `protected override bool Focusable { get; }` |  |
| `HeaderHeight` | `int HeaderHeight { get; }` | The pixel height of one header row. |
| `ImageList` | `ImageList ImageList { get; set; }` | The icons `ImageIndex` indexes into, or `null`. |
| `Panes` | `AccordionPaneCollection Panes { get; }` | The panes, top to bottom. Adding a pane parents it into `Controls`. |
| `SelectedIndex` | `int SelectedIndex { get; set; }` | The index of the current pane — the open one under `Single`, the most recently opened one otherwise; -1 while none is open. Assigning expands that pane through the ordinary path, so `PaneExpanding` can still veto it. |
| `SelectedPane` | `AccordionPane SelectedPane { get; set; }` | The current pane, or `null` while none is open. |
| `GetHeaderBounds` | `Rectangle GetHeaderBounds(int index)` | The client rectangle of the header row of the pane at `index`, or `Empty` for an index outside the stack. Public because aiming a click at a header is otherwise guesswork for callers — tests and UI automation both need it. |

| `OnKeyDown` | `protected override void OnKeyDown(KeyEventArgs e)` |  |
| `OnMouseDown` | `protected override void OnMouseDown(MouseEventArgs e)` |  |
| `OnMouseLeave` | `protected override void OnMouseLeave(EventArgs e)` |  |
| `OnMouseMove` | `protected override void OnMouseMove(MouseEventArgs e)` |  |
| `OnMouseUp` | `protected override void OnMouseUp(MouseEventArgs e)` |  |

#### `AccordionExpandMode`

How many panes of an `Accordion` may be open at once.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Single` | `0` | Outlook-style: expanding a pane collapses every other one, so exactly one body is ever on screen. The default. |
| `Multiple` | `1` | Every pane toggles independently; any number of them can be open, and the open ones share the height left over by the headers. |

#### `AccordionPane`

One pane of an `Accordion`: a `Panel` whose `Text` is the header caption and whose children are the pane body. The owning accordion draws the header, owns the pane's bounds and vetoes its child peers while the pane is collapsed — a pane is never positioned by the Anchor/Dock engine.

Inherits `Panel`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AccordionPane` | `AccordionPane()` | Creates an untitled pane. |
| `AccordionPane` | `AccordionPane(string text)` | Creates a pane with the given header caption. |
| `Expanded` | `bool Expanded { get; set; }` | Whether the pane body is shown. Assigning routes through the owning `Accordion`, so `Single` still collapses the siblings and `PaneExpanding` can still veto. A detached pane just records the flag. |
| `ImageIndex` | `int ImageIndex { get; set; }` | The index of this pane's icon in the owning `ImageList`, or -1 for no icon. The icon is painted between the toggle glyph and the caption. |
| `ImageKey` | `string ImageKey { get; set; }` | The key of this pane's icon in the owning `ImageList`, used when `ImageIndex` is unset (< 0). The index takes precedence when both are set. |
| `OnTextChanged` | `protected override void OnTextChanged(EventArgs e)` |  |

#### `AccordionPaneCancelEventArgs`

Identifies the pane an `Accordion` is about to expand, and lets a handler veto it by setting `Cancel` — the pane then stays closed and no other pane is collapsed on its behalf.

| `Index` | `int Index { get; }` | The pane's index within `Panes`. |
| `Pane` | `AccordionPane Pane { get; }` | The pane about to expand. |

#### `AccordionPaneCollection`

The ordered set of panes owned by an `Accordion`. Adding a pane parents it into the accordion (realizing it immediately when the control is live); removing it tears its peer tree down and hands the selection to a neighbouring pane.

Implements `IEnumerable`, `IEnumerable<AccordionPane>`, `IReadOnlyCollection<AccordionPane>`, `IReadOnlyList<AccordionPane>`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Count` | `int Count { get; }` | The number of panes. |
| `Item` | `AccordionPane this[int index] { get; }` | The pane at the given index. |
| `AddRange` | `void AddRange(params AccordionPane[] panes)` | Appends several panes in order. |
| `Add` | `void Add(AccordionPane pane)` | Appends a pane; the first pane added opens by itself. |
| `Clear` | `void Clear()` | Removes every pane. |
| `GetEnumerator` | `IEnumerator<AccordionPane> GetEnumerator()` |  |
| `IndexOf` | `int IndexOf(AccordionPane pane)` | The index of the pane, or -1 when it is not part of this accordion. |
| `Move` | `void Move(int from, int to)` | Moves the pane at `from` to `to`, keeping it parented and keeping its open/closed state. This list is the order an application saves, so a section the user dragged and one the program placed arrive here by the same route. |
| `Remove` | `bool Remove(AccordionPane pane)` | Removes a pane, disposing its peer tree. Returns whether it was present. |

#### `AnchorStyles`

The container edges a control is bound to (see `Anchor`). When the container resizes, every anchored edge keeps its distance to the matching edge of the container's `DisplayRectangle`: a single anchor translates the control, opposing anchors stretch it, and `None` lets it drift by half the resize delta — the Windows Forms resize model.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `None` | `0` | No edge is bound; the control keeps its position relative to the container's center. |
| `Top` | `1` | The top edge keeps its distance to the container's top. |
| `Bottom` | `2` | The bottom edge keeps its distance to the container's bottom. |
| `Left` | `4` | The left edge keeps its distance to the container's left. |
| `Right` | `8` | The right edge keeps its distance to the container's right. |

#### `Application`

Entry point for a NativeForms UI. Selects a backend, realizes the main form's control tree into native widgets, and pumps the platform message loop — the moral equivalent of `System.Windows.Forms.Application`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PreferNativeWidgets` | `static bool PreferNativeWidgets { get; set; }` | Whether controls that have a faithful platform counterpart realize onto a **real native widget** instead of the owner-drawn surface, when their configured properties stay inside what that widget supports (PRD §12). Defaults to `true`. |
| `Exit` | `static void Exit()` | Requests the running message loop to exit. |
| `Run` | `static void Run(Form mainForm)` | Shows `mainForm` and runs the message loop until it closes, choosing the backend registered for the current platform. |
| `Run` | `static void Run(Form mainForm, IPlatformBackend backend)` | Shows `mainForm` and runs the message loop on an explicit backend. The calling thread becomes the UI thread: its id anchors `InvokeRequired`, and a `NativeFormsSynchronizationContext` is installed on it for the duration of the loop so `await` continuations resume on the loop. |

#### `Appointment`

One scheduled item a `CalendarView` paints: a subject, a start/end instant (or an all-day span), an optional location, a category `Color` and an opaque `Tag` back to the caller's own model. A value type on purpose — the control keeps its bound appointments in one flat array, so a hundred thousand of them cost one allocation rather than a hundred thousand objects, and painting never boxes. The category colour is held as a packed ARGB integer so the struct stays small; `Color` is the value-shaped face of it.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Appointment` | `Appointment(string subject, DateTime start, DateTime end, bool allDay = false, string location = null, Color color = null, object tag = null, bool movable = true)` | Creates an appointment. When `allDay` the time-of-day parts of the bounds are ignored and the item paints in the all-day band / as a month chip. When `movable` is `false` the appointment cannot be dragged to a new time and shows no move affordance — the hook for a locked entry such as a company holiday. |
| `AllDay` | `bool AllDay { get; init; }` | Whether the appointment spans whole days rather than a time range. |
| `Color` | `Color Color { get; init; }` | The category colour of the chip. `Empty` (the default) paints in the theme accent, so an appointment without a category still reads as one. |
| `End` | `DateTime End { get; init; }` | When the appointment ends; treated as at or after `Start`. |
| `Location` | `string Location { get; init; }` | An optional secondary line (a room, a place) shown when the chip is tall enough. |
| `Movable` | `bool Movable { get; init; }` | Whether the user may drag this appointment to a new time. `true` by default; set it `false` on the entries that must not move — a company holiday, a locked booking — so "move all" is the default and "only certain entries" is a matter of locking the rest. A non-movable appointment does not drag and paints no move affordance. |
| `Start` | `DateTime Start { get; init; }` | When the appointment begins. |
| `Subject` | `string Subject { get; init; }` | The one-line title shown on the chip. |
| `Tag` | `object Tag { get; init; }` | Whatever the caller wants to carry back through the events — the source model row. |

#### `AppointmentMoveEventArgs`

Proposes a reschedule of an appointment a `CalendarView` drag produced — a move or an edge resize. It carries the appointment being moved (with its original bounds) and the proposed new `Start`/`End`, snapped to the view's grid. The control owns no storage, so it never mutates the appointment itself: it proposes the change through `AppointmentMoving` (which a handler may `Cancel`) and, if the move stands, reports it through `AppointmentMoved`; the application updates its own model item and re-binds through `SetAppointments` — the same setter/validation idiom the grid uses for an edited cell.

Inherits `EventArgs`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AppointmentMoveEventArgs` | `AppointmentMoveEventArgs(Appointment appointment, DateTime start, DateTime end)` | Proposes a reschedule of an appointment a `CalendarView` drag produced — a move or an edge resize. It carries the appointment being moved (with its original bounds) and the proposed new `Start`/`End`, snapped to the view's grid. The control owns no storage, so it never mutates the appointment itself: it proposes the change through `AppointmentMoving` (which a handler may `Cancel`) and, if the move stands, reports it through `AppointmentMoved`; the application updates its own model item and re-binds through `SetAppointments` — the same setter/validation idiom the grid uses for an edited cell. |
| `Appointment` | `Appointment Appointment { get; }` | The appointment the drag acted on, still carrying its original bounds and its `Tag` back to the caller's model. |
| `Cancel` | `bool Cancel { get; set; }` | Set by an `AppointmentMoving` handler to veto the reschedule. Ignored for `AppointmentMoved`, which reports a move that already stands. |
| `End` | `DateTime End { get; }` | The proposed new end instant, snapped to the view's grid; the duration is preserved on a move and changed on an edge resize. |
| `OriginalEnd` | `DateTime OriginalEnd { get; }` | Where the appointment ended before the drag — a shorthand for `Appointment`.`End`. |
| `OriginalStart` | `DateTime OriginalStart { get; }` | Where the appointment started before the drag — a shorthand for `Appointment`.`Start`. |
| `Start` | `DateTime Start { get; }` | The proposed new start instant, snapped to the view's grid. |

#### `AutoCompleteMode`

How an editable `ComboBox` completes what is typed against its items.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `None` | `0` | No completion: the field holds exactly what was typed. |
| `Suggest` | `1` | The drop-down narrows to the items matching what has been typed so far. |
| `Append` | `2` | The rest of the first matching item is filled into the field and left selected, so the next keystroke replaces it. Deleting never completes, or the text could not be shortened. |
| `SuggestAppend` | `3` | Both — the drop-down narrows and the field completes. |

#### `Breadcrumb`

An Explorer-style breadcrumb bar (§7.9): a row of `BreadcrumbItem` path segments separated by chevrons, each hover-highlit and clickable. When the segments outgrow the width the leading ones fold behind a "…" overflow chip (the trailing path and the last segment always stay visible), so a deep path never spills out of frame. Owner-drawn in the platform theme.

Inherits `OwnerDrawnControl`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Breadcrumb` | `Breadcrumb()` | Creates an empty breadcrumb. |
| `AutoCompleteSource` | `Func<string, IReadOnlyList<string>> AutoCompleteSource { get; set; }` | Supplies path completions for the edit field: given the text typed so far, returns candidate full paths. The first candidate that extends the typed text is appended and selected, so typing on replaces it and Enter accepts it. Delegate-driven, so it completes against a real directory, an archive listing or any virtual namespace. |
| `Editable` | `bool Editable { get; set; }` | Whether clicking the bar's empty space turns it into an editable path field. Off by default; a caller can also drive it explicitly with `BeginEdit`. |
| `Focusable` | `protected override bool Focusable { get; }` |  |
| `FullPath` | `string FullPath { get; }` | The whole path — the segment captions joined by `PathSeparator` — the text the edit field starts from. |
| `ImageList` | `ImageList ImageList { get; set; }` | The icons the segments' `ImageIndex` point into. |
| `IsEditing` | `bool IsEditing { get; }` | Whether the bar is currently showing its edit field rather than the crumbs. |
| `Items` | `BreadcrumbItemCollection Items { get; }` | The path segments, left to right. |
| `PathComposer` | `Func<string> PathComposer { get; set; }` | Supplies the text the edit field starts from. Left `null`, the captions are joined with `PathSeparator`, which is `FullPath`. The counterpart of `PathParser`: a caller that resolves its own paths composes its own too. |
| `PathParser` | `Func<string, IReadOnlyList<BreadcrumbItem>> PathParser { get; set; }` | Turns committed edit text into the new set of segments. Left `null`, the text is split on `PathSeparator` (empty parts dropped). A caller resolving a real or virtual path supplies its own — labelling segments, attaching a `Tag` per node. |
| `PathSeparator` | `string PathSeparator { get; set; }` | The string that joins segments into a path and splits a typed path back into segments — "/" by default. Purely a text convention, so a caller walking an archive or any other virtual namespace picks whatever delimiter that namespace uses. |
| `SubItemsProvider` | `Func<BreadcrumbItem, IReadOnlyList<BreadcrumbItem>> SubItemsProvider { get; set; }` | Supplies the children of a segment for its chevron drop-down — the "folder walk" hook. Given a segment (or `null` for the level before the first one), it returns that node's child entries; a click on the following chevron lists them, and choosing one navigates into it. Nothing here touches the filesystem, so it serves a real directory, an archive or any virtual tree equally. Left `null`, chevrons stay inert separators. |
| `TrimOnClick` | `bool TrimOnClick { get; set; }` | Whether clicking a segment trims the path to it — the classic "navigate up" gesture — before `ItemClicked` is raised. On by default; turn off to keep the whole path and drive navigation entirely from the event. |
| `BeginEdit` | `void BeginEdit()` | Switches the bar to its edit field, prefilled with `PathComposer`'s text or, left unset, `FullPath`, and focused. |
| `EndEdit` | `void EndEdit(bool commit)` | Leaves the edit field. When `commit`, the typed path replaces the segments (through `PathParser`) and `PathEntered` fires; otherwise the crumbs are restored unchanged. |
| `OnItemClicked` | `protected virtual void OnItemClicked(BreadcrumbItemEventArgs e)` | Raises `ItemClicked`. |
| `OnMouseDown` | `protected override void OnMouseDown(MouseEventArgs e)` |  |
| `OnMouseLeave` | `protected override void OnMouseLeave(EventArgs e)` |  |
| `OnMouseMove` | `protected override void OnMouseMove(MouseEventArgs e)` |  |
| `OnPaint` | `protected override void OnPaint(PaintEventArgs e)` |  |
| `OnPathEntered` | `protected virtual void OnPathEntered(BreadcrumbPathEventArgs e)` | Raises `PathEntered`. |
| `OnSubItemSelected` | `protected virtual void OnSubItemSelected(BreadcrumbItemEventArgs e)` | Raises `SubItemSelected`. |
| `ItemClicked` | `event EventHandler<BreadcrumbItemEventArgs> ItemClicked` | Raised when a segment is clicked (after any `TrimOnClick` trim). |
| `PathEntered` | `event EventHandler<BreadcrumbPathEventArgs> PathEntered` | Raised when the edit field commits a path (Enter), carrying the entered text. |

#### `Button`

A push button. Backed by the platform's native button widget, so it looks and behaves exactly like every other button on the user's desktop — and owner-drawn in that platform's own theme for the one face no platform button can express, an image beside a caption (PRD §12).

Inherits `OwnerDrawnControl`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Button` | `Button()` |  |
| `CommandParameter` | `object CommandParameter { get; set; }` | The argument handed to `Command`'s guard and execute delegates. Changing it re-queries the guard. |
| `Command` | `ICommand Command { get; set; }` | The MVVM command a click executes (with `CommandParameter`). Attaching a command puts `Enabled` under its guard: `CanExecute` is applied immediately and re-applied on every `CanExecuteChanged`, so a view-model greys the button out automatically. Setting `null` detaches the subscription and leaves `Enabled` at its last value. |
| `DialogResult` | `DialogResult DialogResult { get; set; }` | The verdict a click reports to the owning `Form`. Anything other than `None` makes a click set `DialogResult`, which in turn closes the form when it is shown modally — exactly the WinForms dialog contract. |
| `FlatStyle` | `FlatStyle FlatStyle { get; set; }` | How the face is drawn. `Standard` and `System` are the platform's own button and keep the widget; `Flat` and `Popup` are faces no platform button offers, so they join `Image` as the promotion gate (§12) and are painted in the desktop's own colours. |
| `Focusable` | `protected override bool Focusable { get; }` | A button takes the keyboard on either path. |
| `ImageAlign` | `ContentAlignment ImageAlign { get; set; }` | Where the image anchors within the button face. Honoured exactly by the painted face; advisory on the widget, which offers no free placement on any backend but is handed the value anyway so a capable one can use it. Defaults to `MiddleCenter`, matching Windows Forms. |
| `Image` | `IImage Image { get; set; }` | The image shown on the button face, or `null` for a text-only button. An image on its own is rendered by the widget, which centres it on all three platforms. An image beside a caption is the promotion gate (§12): none of the three draws both the same way — GTK places the image, a classic Win32 button renders the bitmap alone and drops the caption, AppKit has its own idea — so a captioned image gives up the widget and is painted through the shared `ContentLayout`, which comes out identical everywhere. |
| `IsNativeWidget` | `override bool IsNativeWidget { get; }` |  |
| `TextImageRelation` | `TextImageRelation TextImageRelation { get; set; }` | How image and text share the button face. Honoured exactly by the painted face — which is the half that draws whenever there is both an image and a caption to arrange. On the widget it is advisory: GTK maps the four directional values onto the button's image position (`Overlay` renders as `ImageBeforeText`), and Win32 offers no placement control at all. |
| `IsInputKey` | `protected override bool IsInputKey(Keys keyData)` | Space and Enter work the button rather than reaching the form's accept routing. |
| `OnClick` | `protected override void OnClick(EventArgs e)` | Raises `Click`, executes `Command` when its guard agrees, then reports `DialogResult` to the owning form. |
| `OnKeyUp` | `protected override void OnKeyUp(KeyEventArgs e)` | Space and Enter activate on the key release, like the Windows Forms button base — a held key must not auto-repeat the click. |
| `OnMouseDown` | `protected override void OnMouseDown(MouseEventArgs e)` |  |
| `OnMouseLeave` | `protected override void OnMouseLeave(EventArgs e)` |  |
| `OnMouseMove` | `protected override void OnMouseMove(MouseEventArgs e)` |  |
| `OnMouseUp` | `protected override void OnMouseUp(MouseEventArgs e)` |  |
| `OnPaint` | `protected override void OnPaint(PaintEventArgs e)` |  |
| `OnTextChanged` | `protected override void OnTextChanged(EventArgs e)` |  |

#### `CalendarView`

An owner-drawn, virtualized Outlook-style scheduling surface painted in the native theme — the scheduling counterpart of `MonthCalendar`, which is a date picker. It shows bound `Appointment`s in a `Day`, `WorkWeek`, `Week` or `Month` view: the first three paint a vertical time grid (hour rows on a configurable `TimeScale`, the `WorkDayStart`–`WorkDayEnd` band shaded, a "now" line, and overlapping appointments laid side by side the way Outlook packs a column); the month view paints a six-week day grid with a chip per appointment and a "+n more" overflow marker.

Inherits `OwnerDrawnControl`.

| --- | --- | --- |

| `FirstVisibleDate` | `DateTime FirstVisibleDate { get; }` | The first date the current view shows. |
| `Focusable` | `protected override bool Focusable { get; }` |  |
| `NowLineColor` | `Color NowLineColor { get; set; }` | The colour of the "now" line. Defaults to the shared alert red — no desktop publishes a themed "now" colour to query — so an application can match its own palette. |
| `Now` | `DateTime Now { get; set; }` | The instant the "now" line and the today highlight read. Defaults to `Now`; settable, like `TodayDate`, so long-running views and tests stay deterministic. |
| `SelectedAppointmentIndex` | `int SelectedAppointmentIndex { get; }` | The index of the selected appointment into the start-sorted snapshot, or -1. |
| `SelectedAppointment` | `Appointment? SelectedAppointment { get; }` | The selected appointment, or `null`. |
| `SelectedDate` | `DateTime SelectedDate { get; set; }` | The date the view is centred on: the shown day, the day whose week is shown, or the day whose month is shown. Assigning navigates there. |

| `Previous` | `void Previous()` | Steps the view back one of its own units. |
| `SetAppointments` | `void SetAppointments(IEnumerable<Appointment> appointments)` | Replaces the bound appointments from a ready sequence of `Appointment`s. |
| `SetAppointments` | `void SetAppointments<T>(IEnumerable<T> items, Func<T, Appointment> selector)` | Replaces the bound appointments by projecting each source item through `selector` — the reflection-free binding the grid uses. Takes a start-sorted snapshot; mutating the source afterwards has no effect until the next call. |
| `TryGetAppointmentBounds` | `bool TryGetAppointmentBounds(int index, out Rectangle bounds)` | The client rectangle of the appointment at `index` in the current view, already translated for scroll — the hook the demo and the autopilot aim clicks at. Returns `false` when the appointment is not currently laid out. |

| `AppointmentMoving` | `event EventHandler<AppointmentMoveEventArgs> AppointmentMoving` | Raised while a drag proposes moving or resizing a `Movable` appointment, before it is applied — cancelable. Carries the appointment, its original bounds and the snapped proposed bounds. The control mutates nothing: a handler validates the proposal, updates its own model and re-binds through `SetAppointments`. Setting `Cancel` vetoes the move and the snapshot stays put. |

| `TimeRangeSelected` | `event EventHandler<DateRangeEventArgs> TimeRangeSelected` | Raised when the user click-drags across empty time (or empty month days), carrying the selected span as a `DateRangeEventArgs` — the "new appointment here" hook. |

#### `CalendarViewMode`

Which scheduling surface a `CalendarView` shows, matching the view switch of an Outlook-style calendar. `Day`, `WorkWeek` and `Week` paint a vertical time grid (hour rows, a "now" line, side-by-side overlapping appointments); `Month` paints a day grid with appointment chips per cell.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Day` | `0` | One day as a vertical time grid. |
| `WorkWeek` | `1` | The five work days of the week as adjacent time-grid columns. |
| `Week` | `2` | Seven days from `FirstDayOfWeek` as time-grid columns. |
| `Month` | `3` | The six-week day grid of one month, with appointment chips per day. |

#### `ClockFace`

A material-style analog time picker: a themed dial with a ring of hour numbers, a centre hub and a hand pointing at the selected value. Clicking or dragging the hand onto a number sets that part; the dial advances through stages — `Hour`, then `Minute`, then `Second` while `ShowSeconds` is on — and an `OK` affordance (or Enter on the last stage) commits. A 12-hour dial carries an AM/PM toggle. The control is drawn once in the core and runs on every backend.

Inherits `OwnerDrawnControl`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ClockFace` | `ClockFace()` |  |
| `Cancelled` | `Action Cancelled { get; set; }` | Invoked when the user cancels with Escape. |
| `Committed` | `Action Committed { get; set; }` | Invoked when the user commits: the OK affordance, or Enter on the final stage. |
| `FinalStage` | `ClockFaceStage FinalStage { get; }` | The final stage of the current layout — the deepest hand `Precision` offers. |
| `Focusable` | `protected override bool Focusable { get; }` |  |
| `Invalidated` | `Action Invalidated { get; set; }` | Invoked whenever a host surface needs repainting — the popup-hosting hook, left `null` for a stand-alone control that repaints through its own canvas. |
| `OriginalValue` | `TimeSpan OriginalValue { get; set; }` | The value the dial opened on — a host reverts to it on cancel. Assigning it does not raise `ValueChanged`. |
| `Precision` | `ClockFacePrecision Precision { get; set; }` | How far the dial lets the user drill: hours only, hours+minutes, or hours+minutes+seconds. Lowering it while a now-hidden hand is active falls the stage back to the deepest one still shown. Defaults to `Minutes`. |
| `ShowSeconds` | `bool ShowSeconds { get; set; }` | Whether the dial offers a seconds stage after the minute — the `Precision` value `Seconds` in boolean form. Setting it toggles between `Seconds` and `Minutes`. |
| `Stage` | `ClockFaceStage Stage { get; set; }` | The hand the dial is currently editing. Assigning a stage past the current `Precision` falls back to the deepest hand it offers. |
| `Use24HourClock` | `bool Use24HourClock { get; set; }` | Whether the hour ring runs 00–23 over two rings rather than a single 01–12 ring with an AM/PM toggle. Defaults to `true`, matching `TimePicker`. |
| `Value` | `TimeSpan Value { get; set; }` | The selected time of day — whole seconds, kept inside a single day. Setting it repaints and raises `ValueChanged` when it actually changes. |
| `HandleKeyDown` | `void HandleKeyDown(KeyEventArgs e)` | Keyboard: arrows nudge the active hand, Tab cycles the stage, Enter advances then commits on the last stage, Escape cancels. |
| `HandleMouseDown` | `void HandleMouseDown(ITheme theme, Size size, MouseEventArgs e)` | Reacts to a press: the OK affordance commits, the AM/PM toggle flips the half day, a header segment switches the stage, and a press on the dial begins setting the active part. |

#### `CodeTextBox`

A multiline plain-text code surface: a line-number gutter, a current-line highlight, tab/indent handling, a pluggable delegate `Tokenizer` that colours keyword / string / comment / number spans per line, and an optional `CompletionProvider` autocomplete drop-down. The caret and selection are managed by the control (it owner-draws the text, so colouring stays native-themed). The editing centrepiece an IDE builds on — richer than `RichTextBox`'s flat RTF for source code.

Inherits `OwnerDrawnControl`.

Invoked on Ctrl+Space and as an identifier is typed; picking a candidate replaces the current word. Return an empty list to close the drop-down. |

#### `ColorPicker`

A colour swatch that drops down a full mixer — the toolbar/ribbon/dialog colour chooser. The RGB/HSL/HSV/ CMYK tab picks the whole visual: RGB shows a saturation/value square with a hue bar, HSV a hue ring with an inner square, HSL a hue ring with an inner triangle, and CMYK a colour disc — each beside a value/lightness/ blackness bar and (when `AlphaEnabled`) an alpha bar. There are a hex field, new-versus-current preview, basic/custom swatch palettes, draggable numeric channel sliders and an eyedropper. The face shows the current `SelectedColor` and a chevron; a click opens the light-dismiss mixer, and every edit sets the colour and raises `SelectedColorChanged`.

Inherits `OwnerDrawnControl`.

#### `ComboBox`

A drop-down selector: an owner-drawn field in the native theme whose list opens as a light-dismiss popup (`IPopupPeer`) below the field. Rows are painted by the same renderer as `ListBox` rows — icons, hover highlight, theme selection colors — so the drop-down is pixel-identical to a list. `DropDownList` keeps the field closed and owner-painted; `DropDown` hosts a native `TextBox` over the field area for free-text editing. Items are arbitrary objects; text, icon and value come from reflection-free selector delegates, so binding stays trim/AOT-safe.

Inherits `OwnerDrawnControl`.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `ComboBox` | `ComboBox()` | Creates a combo box in the closed, non-editable `DropDownList` style. |
| `AutoCompleteMode` | `AutoCompleteMode AutoCompleteMode { get; set; }` | How the editable style completes what is typed against the items: not at all (the default), by filling the rest of the first match into the field (`Append`), by narrowing the drop-down to the matches (`Suggest`), or both. |

| `Focusable` | `protected override bool Focusable { get; }` |  |

| `ImageSelector` | `Func<object, IImage> ImageSelector { get; set; }` | Optional selector producing an icon for an item; `null` for none. |
| `IsNativeWidget` | `override bool IsNativeWidget { get; }` | Whether this combo is currently rendered by a real platform widget. |
| `Items` | `ObservableList<object> Items { get; }` | The items offered by the drop-down. Mutating this collection repaints the control. |
| `MaxDropDownItems` | `int MaxDropDownItems { get; set; }` | The maximum number of rows the drop-down shows before it scrolls. Defaults to 8. |
| `PlaceholderText` | `string PlaceholderText { get; set; }` | The greyed hint shown while nothing is selected (closed style) or the editor is empty. |

Base class for the native common dialogs (`OpenFileDialog`, `ColorDialog` …). A dialog object is a thin option holder: `ShowDialog` hands the options to the running backend, which presents the platform's own dialog application-modal and blocks until it closes.

#### `ContextMenuStrip`

A context menu: the same item model and owner-drawn drop-down engine as a `MenuStrip` drop-down, opened at an arbitrary screen point instead of below a bar. Assign one to `ContextMenuStrip` and a right-click on an owner-drawn control opens it at the cursor; `Show` opens it programmatically. It is a component, not a control — it owns no peer until it opens and can serve any number of controls at once.

Inherits `Component`. Implements `IDisposable`.

Off by default, because it costs the menu its mnemonics: type-to-filter and mnemonic access are the same keystrokes, so one menu cannot offer both. |
| `Close` | `void Close()` | Closes the menu, if open. |
| `Dispose` | `protected override void Dispose(bool disposing)` | Closes the menu and drops the drop-down engine (and with it the native popups). |
| `OnOpening` | `protected virtual void OnOpening(CancelEventArgs e)` | Raises `Opening`. |

| `Closed` | `event EventHandler Closed` | Raised after the menu (and its whole cascade) has closed. |
| `Opening` | `event EventHandler<CancelEventArgs> Opening` | Raised before the menu opens — on the right-click path through `ContextMenuStrip` and on explicit `Show` alike; set `Cancel` to keep it closed. |

#### `Control`

Base class for every visual element. The API mirrors `System.Windows.Forms.Control` closely enough that porting is mostly a namespace swap: absolute `Bounds` in parent-client pixels, a `Controls` child collection, and familiar `Click`/ `TextChanged` events.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Control` | `protected Control()` |  |
| `AccessibleDescription` | `string AccessibleDescription { get; set; }` | A longer description announced after the name, for what the name cannot carry. |
| `AccessibleName` | `string AccessibleName { get; set; }` | What assistive technology calls this control. Unset, it falls back to `DefaultAccessibleName`, which is the control's own text for anything that has one. |
| `AccessibleRole` | `AccessibleRole AccessibleRole { get; set; }` | What this control is, announced after its name. Unset, it falls back to `DefaultAccessibleRole`, which every control overrides to say what it is. |
| `AllowDrop` | `bool AllowDrop { get; set; }` | Whether this control accepts in-process drag-and-drop: only opted-in controls are considered by the hit-test a drag performs, and only they raise `DragEnter`/ `DragOver`/`DragLeave`/`DragDrop`. |
| `Anchor` | `AnchorStyles Anchor { get; set; }` | The container edges this control is bound to, `Top` \| `Left` by default. When the parent resizes, every anchored edge keeps its distance to the matching edge of the parent's `DisplayRectangle`: opposing anchors stretch the control, a single anchor translates it, and `None` drifts by half the delta. Assigning an anchor resets `Dock` to `None` — the two are mutually exclusive and the property assigned last wins, exactly like Windows Forms. |
| `BackColor` | `Color BackColor { get; set; }` | The background color — ambient like `Font`: unset controls inherit from the parent chain, then the theme. `ResetBackColor` returns to the ambient value. |
| `Bounds` | `Rectangle Bounds { get; set; }` | Position and size relative to the parent's client area, in pixels. |
| `CanFocus` | `bool CanFocus { get; }` | Whether `Focus` would succeed right now: the control kind takes focus at all, the control is visible and enabled, and a native peer exists to receive it. |
| `ContextMenuStrip` | `ContextMenuStrip ContextMenuStrip { get; set; }` | The context menu a right-click on this control opens at the cursor, or `null` for none. Owner-drawn controls open it from their mouse pipeline; native-widget controls open it from their peer's `ContextMenuRequested`. |
| `Controls` | `ControlCollection Controls { get; }` | The child controls hosted by this control. Created on first access, so the many leaf controls that never host children pay no collection allocation — internal traversals go through `ChildrenOrNull` and skip the empty case. |
| `Cursor` | `Cursor Cursor { get; set; }` | The pointer shape shown over the control — ambient like `Font`: unset controls inherit from the parent chain, then `Arrow`. `ResetCursor` returns to the ambient value. |
| `DisplayRectangle` | `virtual Rectangle DisplayRectangle { get; }` | The client rectangle available to content: the full client area deflated by `Padding`. Containers with chrome of their own (a `GroupBox` frame) deflate further. |
| `Dock` | `DockStyle Dock { get; set; }` | The parent edge this control glues itself to, `None` by default. Docked siblings claim their edges of the parent's `DisplayRectangle` in reverse `Controls` order — the last-added sibling docks first — each shrinking the rectangle left for the next; `Fill` takes whatever remains. Assigning a dock resets `Anchor` to its default — the property assigned last wins, exactly like Windows Forms. |
| `Enabled` | `bool Enabled { get; set; }` | Whether the widget accepts user interaction. The getter is effective, exactly like Windows Forms: a control inside a disabled ancestor reports `false` even while its own flag is still set. The setter only writes this control's own flag; the peer receives the local value — native widgets grey out with their disabled parent already. |
| `Focusable` | `protected virtual bool Focusable { get; }` | Whether this kind of control can take keyboard focus at all. Interactive native widgets (buttons, text boxes) can; static kinds (`Label`) and non-interactive owner-drawn surfaces override to `false`. |
| `Focused` | `bool Focused { get; }` | Whether the peer currently holds keyboard focus, tracked from its focus events. |
| `Font` | `Font Font { get; set; }` | The font the control's text renders in — an ambient property: unset controls inherit the nearest ancestor's font and finally the theme's default, exactly like Windows Forms. `ResetFont` returns an explicitly set control to the ambient value. |
| `ForeColor` | `Color ForeColor { get; set; }` | The text color — ambient like `Font`: unset controls inherit from the parent chain, then the theme. `ResetForeColor` returns to the ambient value. |
| `Height` | `int Height { get; set; }` | The height in pixels. |
| `InvokeRequired` | `bool InvokeRequired { get; }` | Whether the caller must marshal through `Invoke`/`BeginInvoke` to touch this control: `true` only while a message loop is running on another thread. `false` outside `Run`, matching the WinForms convention for a control without a created handle. |
| `IsNativeWidget` | `virtual bool IsNativeWidget { get; }` | Forces this control onto a real platform widget (`true`) or onto the owner-drawn painter (`false`); `null` — the default — follows `PreferNativeWidgets`. Controls that have no platform counterpart ignore it entirely (PRD §12). |
| `Left` | `int Left { get; set; }` | The x-coordinate of the left edge. |
| `Location` | `Point Location { get; set; }` | The top-left corner of `Bounds`. |
| `Margin` | `Padding Margin { get; set; }` | The spacing layout containers (`FlowLayoutPanel`, `TableLayoutPanel`) keep around this control. Plain containers position children by `Bounds` alone and ignore it. |
| `Name` | `string Name { get; set; }` | The programmatic name of the control — designer-style lookup data, never rendered. Defaults to the empty string; assigning `null` resets to it. |
| `Padding` | `Padding Padding { get; set; }` | The interior spacing between the control's edges and its content, in pixels per side. Not ambient (each control owns its padding); owner-drawn controls honor it through `DisplayRectangle` and their content layout. |
| `Parent` | `Control Parent { get; }` | The containing control, or `null` for a top-level form. |
| `RightToLeft` | `RightToLeft RightToLeft { get; set; }` | The text direction, `Inherit` by default: the effective value comes from the nearest ancestor with an explicit setting, falling back to `No`. When it resolves to `Yes` owner-drawn controls mirror their glyph/text painting and a container mirrors where its children physically sit — the logical `Bounds` stay left-to-right, only the peer placement flips across the client width. |
| `Size` | `Size Size { get; set; }` | The size of `Bounds`. |
| `TabIndex` | `int TabIndex { get; set; }` | The position of this control in its container's tab order. Siblings are visited in ascending `TabIndex` (ties keep the `Controls` insertion order), depth-first through nested containers — the Windows Forms traversal. Defaults to 0. |
| `TabStop` | `bool TabStop { get; set; }` | Whether Tab stops on this control. Until assigned it follows the per-kind default: focusable controls are tab stops, static and container kinds (labels, panels, group boxes, picture boxes, progress bars, scroll bars, strips) are not, and the menu bar opts out because Alt — not Tab — reaches it, matching Windows Forms. |

| `Text` | `virtual string Text { get; set; }` | The caption text: a button label, a form's title bar, a label's text. |
| `Top` | `int Top { get; set; }` | The y-coordinate of the top edge. |
| `UseNativeWidget` | `bool? UseNativeWidget { get; set; }` |  |
| `Visible` | `bool Visible { get; set; }` | Whether the widget is shown. The getter is effective, exactly like Windows Forms: a control inside a hidden ancestor reports `false` even while its own flag is still set. A container that hides its content wholesale without touching the children's flags — a collapsed `Expander`, a collapsed `SplitContainer` panel — counts as such an ancestor: its veto (`GetChildPeerVisible`) is what the peer obeys, so reporting anything else here would contradict the pixels. The setter only writes this control's own flag; the peer receives the local value — native widget nesting already hides children with their parent. |
| `Width` | `int Width { get; set; }` | The width in pixels. |
| `BeginInvoke` | `void BeginInvoke(Action action)` | Queues `action` for execution on the UI thread and returns immediately. Callable from any thread. |
| `CurrentFrameOf` | `protected IImage CurrentFrameOf(IImage image)` | Resolves an image to the frame to paint now: an `AnimatedImage` yields its current frame — frozen and greyed while the control is disabled — and a still image yields itself. Draw or push this rather than the raw image so an animated image assigned to a plain image property animates. |
| `DoDragDrop` | `void DoDragDrop(object data, DragDropEffects allowedEffects)` | Starts an in-process drag with this control as the source. The call returns immediately — unlike WinForms there is no nested message loop — and the drag then follows the source's captured mouse stream: targets with `AllowDrop` receive `DragEnter`/ `DragOver`/`DragLeave`, and releasing the button raises `DragDrop` on the target that accepted an effect. The source must be a realized `OwnerDrawnControl` (only those own a mouse stream); in-process only — OS-level drag sources and drop targets are tracked in `docs/PRD.md` §8. |
| `FindForm` | `Form FindForm()` | The form this control sits on — itself for a form — or `null` while unparented. |
| `Focus` | `void Focus()` | Moves keyboard focus to this control by asking the peer (`SetFocus` on Win32, `gtk_widget_grab_focus` on GTK). A no-op while `CanFocus` is `false`; `Focused` flips when the platform reports the change. On a composite the focus lands on its `FocusTarget`. |
| `Invalidate` | `virtual void Invalidate()` | Requests a full repaint. Owner-drawn controls forward to their canvas surface; controls backed by a native widget repaint themselves through the platform and treat this as a no-op — `IControlPeer` exposes no invalidation seam. |
| `Invalidate` | `virtual void Invalidate(Rectangle region)` | Requests a repaint of a client-space sub-region (see `Invalidate`). |
| `Invoke` | `void Invoke(Action action)` | Executes `action` on the UI thread and blocks until it completed. On the UI thread (or with no loop running) it runs inline; from any other thread it is queued onto the loop and awaited. Exceptions propagate to the caller either way. |
| `IsInputKey` | `protected virtual bool IsInputKey(Keys keyData)` | Whether the control claims `keyData` for its own input, exempting the key from the owning form's dialog handling (Tab navigation, Enter → `AcceptButton`, Escape → `CancelButton`). The base claims nothing; controls that consume Enter or Escape themselves — an open drop-down, a grid edit — override this. |
| `LogicalToDevice` | `Size LogicalToDevice(Size size)` | Scales a logical size to device pixels, component-wise. |
| `LogicalToDevice` | `int LogicalToDevice(int value)` | Scales a logical (96-DPI) pixel length to device pixels using the backend's current DPI scale, rounding to the nearest pixel. Identity before realization — an unrealized control has no monitor to scale for. |

Deferred while suspended, swallowed while a pass is already running (the bounds writes of a pass re-enter here through the child hooks). |

| `Leave` | `event EventHandler Leave` | Raised when focus leaves the control — and, on containers, when focus leaves their subtree entirely. On the control itself it follows `LostFocus`. |

Delivered for owner-drawn controls (buttons, lists, custom surfaces); native widgets consume their own presses, so the button press does not surface for them — the same platform limit documented for native key preview. |
| `MouseEnter` | `event EventHandler MouseEnter` | Raised when the pointer enters this control's bounds (the first move after a leave). |
| `MouseLeave` | `event EventHandler MouseLeave` | Raised when the pointer leaves this control — the counterpart of `MouseEnter`. |
| `MouseMove` | `event EventHandler<MouseEventArgs> MouseMove` | Raised while the pointer moves over this control — native widgets and owner-drawn surfaces alike. |
| `MouseUp` | `event EventHandler<MouseEventArgs> MouseUp` | Raised when a mouse button is released over this control (owner-drawn controls). |

| `TextChanged` | `event EventHandler TextChanged` | Raised after `Text` changes. |

#### `ControlCollection`

The ordered set of child controls owned by a `Control`. Mirrors `Control.ControlCollection`: adding a control re-parents it (and realizes it immediately when the owner is already live), removing it clears the parent and tears down its native peers.

Implements `IEnumerable`, `IEnumerable<Control>`, `IReadOnlyCollection<Control>`, `IReadOnlyList<Control>`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Count` | `int Count { get; }` | The number of child controls. |
| `Item` | `Control this[int index] { get; }` | The child control at the given index. |
| `AddRange` | `void AddRange(params Control[] controls)` | Adds several controls in order. For absolutely-placed or anchored children this is linear (the base `OnChildAdded` lays out only for a docked child); a layout panel that positions its own children re-flows per add, so wrap a large batch into it in `SuspendLayout`/`ResumeLayout` to keep it linear. |
| `Add` | `void Add(Control control)` | Adds a control and sets its `Parent` to the owner. When the owner is already realized as a container, the control (and its subtree) realizes immediately. |
| `Clear` | `void Clear()` | Removes every child, clearing their parents and disposing their peer trees. |
| `Contains` | `bool Contains(Control control)` | Whether the control is a direct child. |
| `GetEnumerator` | `IEnumerator<Control> GetEnumerator()` |  |
| `Remove` | `bool Remove(Control control)` | Removes a control, clears its parent and disposes its peer tree, returning the control to its unrealized (but re-realizable) shape. Returns whether it was present. |

#### `Cursor`

A pointer shape, the moral equivalent of `System.Windows.Forms.Cursor` reduced to the stock set every platform ships: it names a `CursorKind` and the backend resolves it to the native cursor (`LoadCursorW(IDC_*)` on Win32, `gdk_cursor_new_from_name` on GTK). Stock instances come from `Cursors`; a custom bitmap pointer comes from `FromBytes` — a decoded `.cur`/`.ani`/icon with its hotspot — which the backend turns into a native cursor (`gdk_cursor_new_from_pixbuf` on GTK, `CreateIconIndirect` on Win32).

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Kind` | `CursorKind Kind { get; }` | The stock shape this cursor renders as, or `Custom` for a bitmap. |
| `FromBytes` | `static Cursor FromBytes(ReadOnlySpan<byte> data)` | Builds a custom cursor from image bytes: a `.cur` (its hotspot is honoured), an animated `.ani` (its first frame), an `.ico` or any still image (hotspot at the top-left). Assign the result to `Cursor` or `Cursors`-style usage. |
| `FromImage` | `static Cursor FromImage(int[] pixels, int width, int height, int hotspotX = 0, int hotspotY = 0)` | Builds a custom cursor directly from row-major ARGB pixels and a hotspot. |

#### `DataGridView`

An owner-drawn, vertically virtualized data grid painted in the native theme. Rows are arbitrary objects bound through an `ObservableList`; each `DataGridViewColumn` maps a row to its cell content via reflection-free selector delegates, so binding stays trim/AOT-safe. Columns render as text, check, button, link, multi-image, progress, color, list or checked-list cells (`DataGridViewColumnKind`), headers sort through an index indirection that never mutates `Items`, and presentation (row colors/heights/visibility, cell styles, display formatting, cell tooltips) is driven by optional per-row/per-cell selectors. Cells edit in place through `BeginEdit` — a hosted editor, popup or dialog per `DataGridViewColumnKind`, entered per `EditMode`, with Tab/Enter walking the editable cells — columns can be frozen, fill-sized by weight, drag-reordered through a display-order indirection and copied to (or pasted from, via `Paste`) the clipboard as tab-separated text, `MultiSelect` extends the full-row selection to Ctrl/Shift sets, and overflowing content grows interactive scrollbar strips along the grid's edges.

Inherits `OwnerDrawnControl`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DataGridView` | `DataGridView()` | Creates a data grid. |
| `AllowUserToFilterColumns` | `bool AllowUserToFilterColumns { get; set; }` | Whether each column header offers a filter: a funnel glyph that opens the column's distinct display values as a searchable, checkable menu (PRD §14). Defaults to `false`. |
| `AllowUserToOrderColumns` | `bool AllowUserToOrderColumns { get; set; }` | Whether dragging a column header past a neighbor reorders the display: the drag rewrites `DisplayIndex` on every column while `Columns` keeps its model order. Defaults to `false`. |
| `AllowUserToResizeColumns` | `bool AllowUserToResizeColumns { get; set; }` | Whether dragging a column divider in the header resizes that column. Defaults to `true`; the grab zone is ±3 px around the divider. |
| `AlternatingRowColor` | `Color AlternatingRowColor { get; set; }` | The background tint of alternating rows when `AlternatingRows` is enabled. |
| `AlternatingRows` | `bool AlternatingRows { get; set; }` | Whether every other data row is tinted with `AlternatingRowColor`. |
| `ColumnHeaderHeight` | `int ColumnHeaderHeight { get; set; }` | The pixel height of the column-header row. Defaults to `RowHeight`. |
| `Columns` | `IList<DataGridViewColumn> Columns { get; }` | The columns shown. Mutate then call `Invalidate` to repaint. |
| `CurrentColumnIndex` | `int CurrentColumnIndex { get; set; }` | The column index keyboard activation (Space/Enter) targets; follows the last clicked cell. |
| `DataSource` | `IEnumerable DataSource { set; }` | Replaces the rows from any sequence (one-way binding convenience). |
| `EditMode` | `DataGridViewEditMode EditMode { get; set; }` | How cells enter edit mode. Defaults to `EditOnKeystrokeOrF2`. |
| `EditingControl` | `Control EditingControl { get; }` | The hosted editor control while a `Text`, `MaskedText`, `NumericUpDown` or `DomainUpDown` cell is in edit mode, or `null` (popup- and dialog-based kinds host no child control). |
| `Focusable` | `protected override bool Focusable { get; }` |  |
| `FullRowTextSelector` | `Func<object, string> FullRowTextSelector { get; set; }` | Optional selector merging a row into one full-width cell: a row whose result is non-`null` paints that text across every column (a group or separator row) and is skipped by selection, navigation and editing. Runs on the paint path — return a cached string, capture nothing. |
| `HeaderHeight` | `protected int HeaderHeight { get; }` | The pixel height of the column-header row, or 0 when hidden. |
| `HorizontalOffset` | `int HorizontalOffset { get; set; }` | The horizontal scroll offset in pixels, clamped so the non-frozen columns never scroll past their total width; they are shifted left by this amount while frozen columns stay put. |
| `IsCurrentCellDirty` | `bool IsCurrentCellDirty { get; }` | Whether the hosted editor's content has changed since the edit began — cleared when the edit ends. Popup-based kinds commit through their pick gesture and never report dirty. |
| `IsEditing` | `bool IsEditing { get; }` | Whether a cell is currently in edit mode. |
| `IsHorizontalScrollBarVisible` | `bool IsHorizontalScrollBarVisible { get; }` | Whether the horizontal scrollbar strip is currently shown (the columns overflow the viewport). |
| `IsVerticalScrollBarVisible` | `bool IsVerticalScrollBarVisible { get; }` | Whether the vertical scrollbar strip is currently shown (the rows overflow the viewport). |

Defaults to `false`. |

| `RowHeightSelector` | `Func<object, int?> RowHeightSelector { get; set; }` | Optional per-row pixel height over the row item; `null` (selector or result) uses `RowHeight`. Evaluated linearly over the visible window only. |
| `RowHeight` | `int RowHeight { get; set; }` | The pixel height of a data row. Defaults to the theme row height. |
| `RowHiddenSelector` | `Func<object, bool> RowHiddenSelector { get; set; }` | Optional predicate hiding rows; hidden rows are skipped by painting, hit-testing and keyboard navigation. Evaluated linearly over the visible window only. |
| `RowSelectableSelector` | `Func<object, bool> RowSelectableSelector { get; set; }` | Optional predicate over the row item deciding whether the row can be selected via mouse or keyboard; `null` means all rows are selectable. |

| `SelectedItems` | `IEnumerable<object> SelectedItems { get; }` | The selected row items in model order: the whole Ctrl/Shift set while `MultiSelect` has built one, otherwise the single selected row. |

Stable while the grid is sorted — sorting only reorders the presentation. Assigning collapses a multi-selection to the one row. |
| `ShowCellToolTips` | `bool ShowCellToolTips { get; set; }` | Whether resting the pointer on a cell whose column has a `TooltipSelector` pops that text up near the cursor. Defaults to `true`. |
| `ShowColumnHeaders` | `bool ShowColumnHeaders { get; set; }` | Whether the column-header row is painted. Defaults to `true`. |
| `ShowGridLines` | `bool ShowGridLines { get; set; }` | Whether grid lines are painted. Defaults to `true`. |
| `ShowRowHeaders` | `bool ShowRowHeaders { get; set; }` | Whether a header column is painted at the left edge, with a marker triangle on the selected row. Defaults to `false`. |

| `VirtualMode` | `bool VirtualMode { get; set; }` | Whether rows are served on demand by `RetrieveVirtualRow` over a `VirtualRowCount` instead of from `Items`, so a million-row query never materialises. Sorting is left to the data source while virtual (the grid cannot compare rows it has not fetched), and `Items` is ignored. Defaults to `false`. |
| `VirtualRowCount` | `int VirtualRowCount { get; set; }` | The row count exposed while `VirtualMode` is on, or `-1` for an unknown size: the grid then probes past what it has confirmed, growing as you scroll until `RetrieveVirtualRow` reports the end. |

Refused (returning `false`) for read-only cells, kinds without their edit selectors/setters, merged or hidden rows, cells outside the visible window, a veto from `CellBeginEdit`, or popup kinds before realization. An edit already active on another cell is committed first; its validation veto also refuses the new edit. |

For the single-value popup kinds — which commit through their own pick gestures — this closes the popup without a write; for the set-valued ones it is the commit, writing everything the popup has ticked through `CheckedItemsSetter`. A no-op returning `true` while nothing edits. |

Indices are model indices. |

Empty without a selection. Ctrl+C puts exactly this on the system clipboard through the backend. |
| `GetFilterValues` | `IReadOnlyList<string> GetFilterValues(DataGridViewColumn column)` | The distinct values a column displays, in first-seen order, as the filter menu offers them. | `OnMouseUp` | `protected override void OnMouseUp(MouseEventArgs e)` |  |
| `OnMouseWheel` | `protected override void OnMouseWheel(MouseEventArgs e)` |  |
| `OnPaint` | `protected override void OnPaint(PaintEventArgs e)` |  |
| `OnPasteCompleted` | `protected virtual void OnPasteCompleted(EventArgs e)` | Raises `PasteCompleted`. |
| `OnRowValidated` | `protected virtual void OnRowValidated(DataGridViewCellEventArgs e)` | Raises `RowValidated`. |
| `OnRowValidating` | `protected virtual void OnRowValidating(DataGridViewCellCancelEventArgs e)` | Raises `RowValidating`. |
| `OnSelectionChanged` | `protected virtual void OnSelectionChanged(EventArgs e)` | Raises `SelectionChanged`. |
| `Paste` | `void Paste(string text)` | Pastes tab-separated text into the grid starting at the current cell: lines map onto display rows from the current row downward (skipping hidden, unselectable and merged rows), cells onto display columns from the current column rightward; content past the last column or row is dropped. Each target cell converts its text to the column kind's value and writes through that kind's setter — read-only cells, display-only columns and unparseable text are skipped, their position still consumed, and every write runs `CellValidating` first (a veto skips that one cell). `PasteCompleted` closes the operation. Ctrl+V feeds this from the system clipboard through the backend. A no-op without a current cell. |
| `SetColumnFilter` | `void SetColumnFilter(DataGridViewColumn column, IReadOnlyCollection<string> accepted)` | Applies a column's accepted values and re-lays the grid out. A set covering every value the column shows is stored as no filter at all, so the header glyph stops claiming one is active. |
| `Sort` | `void Sort(DataGridViewColumn column, SortOrder order)` | Sorts the presentation by the given column and direction, or clears the sort when `column` is `null` or `order` is `None`. Sorting reorders an index indirection — `Items` is never mutated — rebuilt lazily after item changes. |
| `CellBeginEdit` | `event EventHandler<DataGridViewCellCancelEventArgs> CellBeginEdit` | Raised before a cell enters edit mode; setting `Cancel` keeps it read. |
| `CellClick` | `event EventHandler<DataGridViewCellEventArgs> CellClick` | Raised when a data cell is clicked, and on Space/Enter for the current cell. |
| `CellContentClick` | `event EventHandler<DataGridViewCellEventArgs> CellContentClick` | Raised when the content of a check, button, link or multi-image cell is clicked; for multi-image cells `ContentIndex` names the icon. |
| `CellDoubleClick` | `event EventHandler<DataGridViewCellEventArgs> CellDoubleClick` | Raised when a data cell is clicked twice in quick succession. |
| `CellEndEdit` | `event EventHandler<DataGridViewCellEventArgs> CellEndEdit` | Raised after a cell leaves edit mode, whether the edit committed or was cancelled. |
| `CellItemCheck` | `event EventHandler<ItemCheckEventArgs> CellItemCheck` | Raised before an item's tick flips inside the popup of a `CheckedListBox` cell — the grid-side sibling of `ItemCheck`, with the same veto shape: a handler resets `NewValue` to `CurrentValue` to keep the tick as it was. `Index` indexes the popup's item list; the cell it belongs to is the one `SelectedRowIndex`/`CurrentColumnIndex` report while the popup is open. Only the popup's own ticks raise it — the whole set still commits through `CheckedItemsSetter` afterwards. |
| `CellValidating` | `event EventHandler<DataGridViewCellValidatingEventArgs> CellValidating` | Raised before an edit commits, carrying the proposed value; setting `Cancel` vetoes the write and keeps the cell in edit mode. |
| `ColumnFilterChanged` | `event EventHandler<DataGridViewCellEventArgs> ColumnFilterChanged` | Raised after a column's filter changed, whether from the menu or from code. |
| `CurrentCellDirtyStateChanged` | `event EventHandler CurrentCellDirtyStateChanged` | Raised when `IsCurrentCellDirty` flips — on the first editor change after the edit begins, and again when the edit ends. |
| `PasteCompleted` | `event EventHandler PasteCompleted` | Raised after `Paste` processed clipboard text — every attempted cell already ran its own `CellValidating`. |
| `RetrieveVirtualRow` | `event EventHandler<RetrieveVirtualRowEventArgs> RetrieveVirtualRow` | Raised while `VirtualMode` is on to fetch the row item at an index. Called once per visible row per paint — keep it cheap. |
| `RowValidated` | `event EventHandler<DataGridViewCellEventArgs> RowValidated` | Raised after the current row was left without a `RowValidating` veto. |
| `RowValidating` | `event EventHandler<DataGridViewCellCancelEventArgs> RowValidating` | Raised before the current row is left for another one, carrying the row being left; setting `Cancel` keeps the selection where it is. |
| `SelectionChanged` | `event EventHandler SelectionChanged` | Raised when `SelectedRowIndex` changes. |

#### `DataGridViewAutoSizeColumnMode`

How a `DataGridViewColumn` computes its width.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `None` | `0` | The width is whatever `Width` says. The default. |
| `AllCells` | `1` | The width fits the widest cell text currently in the visible row window, remeasured on demand each paint. Deliberately window-scoped: measuring all rows would defeat virtualization, so the width may adapt as the grid scrolls. |
| `Fill` | `2` | The column shares the viewport width left over after the fixed columns with the other fill columns, proportionally to `FillWeight` and floored at `MinimumWidth`; recomputed whenever the grid's size changes. |

Row indices refer to `Items` (the model order), so they stay stable while the grid is sorted. |

Carries the value a `DataGridView` edit is about to commit (`CellValidating`): the edited text for a `Text` cell, the `Decimal` for a `NumericUpDown` cell, the chosen item for a `ComboBox` cell and the `DateTime` for a `DateTime` cell. Setting `Cancel` vetoes the commit and keeps the cell in edit mode. Row indices refer to `Items` (the model order), so they stay stable while the grid is sorted.

Setting `Cancel` vetoes the commit and keeps the cell in edit mode. Row indices refer to `Items` (the model order), so they stay stable while the grid is sorted. |

#### `DataGridViewColumn`

A column definition for a `DataGridView`. Cell values are produced by reflection-free selector delegates (row item → value / icon / state), so binding stays trim/AOT-safe. One class covers every `DataGridViewColumnKind` — the kind-specific selectors are simply unused by the other kinds — which keeps the grid's paint switch free of per-cell objects.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DataGridViewColumn` | `DataGridViewColumn(string headerText, Func<object, object> valueSelector)` | Creates a column bound to the given value selector. |
| `Alignment` | `ContentAlignment Alignment { get; set; }` | Alignment of the cell content within the column. |
| `AutoSizeMode` | `DataGridViewAutoSizeColumnMode AutoSizeMode { get; set; }` | How the column width is computed. Defaults to `None`. |
| `CellStyleSelector` | `Func<object, DataGridViewCellStyle> CellStyleSelector { get; set; }` | Optional per-cell style overrides (colors, alignment); `null` keeps the defaults. Returns a value type, so it is safe on the paint path. |
| `CheckedItemsSelector` | `Func<object, IReadOnlyList<object>> CheckedItemsSelector { get; set; }` | Maps a row item to the items currently in the set of a `CheckedListBox` — or multi-select `ListBox` — cell. The cell's text is those items' display texts joined with `", "`, cached per row, so the selector never runs on the paint path. |
| `CheckedItemsSetter` | `Action<object, IReadOnlyList<object>> CheckedItemsSetter { get; set; }` | Writes the whole picked set back to the row item when a `CheckedListBox` — or multi-select `ListBox` — cell commits. The grid hands over a freshly allocated array holding the picked items in `ItemsSelector` order and keeps no reference to it, so the setter may store it as-is. |
| `CheckedSelector` | `Func<object, bool> CheckedSelector { get; set; }` | Maps a row item to the check state of a `Check` cell; unset cells render unchecked. |
| `CheckedSetter` | `Action<object, bool> CheckedSetter { get; set; }` | Writes the toggled check state back to the row item when a `Check` cell is clicked and the cell is not read-only; `null` makes the glyph display-only. |
| `ColorSelector` | `Func<object, Color> ColorSelector { get; set; }` | Maps a row item to the swatch color of a `Color` cell; required (with `ColorSetter`) for the cell to edit. |
| `ColorSetter` | `Action<object, Color> ColorSetter { get; set; }` | Writes the color picked in the native color dialog back to the row item when a `Color` cell edits. |
| `DateSelector` | `Func<object, DateTime> DateSelector { get; set; }` | Maps a row item to the date a `DateTime` editor's popup calendar starts on. |
| `DateSetter` | `Action<object, DateTime> DateSetter { get; set; }` | Writes the day picked in a `DateTime` editor back to the row item; the time of day of the `DateSelector` value is preserved. |
| `DecimalPlaces` | `int DecimalPlaces { get; set; }` | The number of decimal digits the `NumericUpDown` editor displays (0–28). |
| `DisplayIndex` | `int DisplayIndex { get; set; }` | The column's position in the display order, or a negative value (the default) for its position in `Columns`. A drag-reorder gesture rewrites it on every column; assigning it directly reorders the presentation on the next repaint — `Columns` itself is never reordered. |
| `DisplayTextSelector` | `Func<object, string> DisplayTextSelector { get; set; }` | Optional override of the displayed cell text; return `null` to fall back to `ValueSelector`. |
| `EnabledSelector` | `Func<object, bool> EnabledSelector { get; set; }` | Maps a row item to whether a `Button` cell is enabled; `null` means always enabled. Disabled buttons grey their text and raise no `CellContentClick`. |
| `FillWeight` | `float FillWeight { get; set; }` | The column's share of the leftover viewport width under `Fill`, relative to the other fill columns' weights. Kept above zero. |
| `Filter` | `IReadOnlyCollection<string> Filter { get; set; }` | The display values this column accepts, or `null` when it filters nothing. A row shows only while every filtered column accepts the text that column displays for it. |
| `FormatSelector` | `Func<object, string> FormatSelector { get; set; }` | Optional formatter over the `ValueSelector` result — the reflection-free `CellFormatting` seam: it runs after the value selector and shapes the displayed text only, so editors still seed from the raw value. Its result is cached per cell until the row changes, so it never runs per frame. |
| `Frozen` | `bool Frozen { get; set; }` | Whether the column is pinned at the left edge: frozen columns form the leading run of the display order and stay put while `HorizontalOffset` scrolls the rest underneath them. |
| `HeaderText` | `string HeaderText { get; set; }` | The text painted in the column header. |
| `ImageGap` | `int ImageGap { get; set; }` | The gap between adjacent icons in a `MultiImage` cell. Defaults to `4`. |
| `ImagePadding` | `int ImagePadding { get; set; }` | The inset from the cell edges for a `MultiImage` cell's icon strip. Defaults to `2`. |
| `ImageSelector` | `Func<object, IImage> ImageSelector { get; set; }` | Optional selector producing a per-cell icon painted beside the text; `null` for none. `TextImageRelation` decides which side. |
| `ImageSize` | `Size ImageSize { get; set; }` | The fixed box the cell icon is drawn into, or `Empty` (the default) to size it to the row height. See `KeepImageAspectRatio`. |
| `ImageTooltipSelector` | `Func<object, int, string> ImageTooltipSelector { get; set; }` | Optional per-icon tooltip for a `MultiImage` cell, taking the row item and the icon index; `null` falls back to `TooltipSelector`. |
| `ImagesSelector` | `Func<object, IReadOnlyList<IImage>> ImagesSelector { get; set; }` | Maps a row item to the icons of a `MultiImage` cell, painted side by side. Return a cached list — the selector runs on the paint path. |
| `Increment` | `decimal Increment { get; set; }` | The step of the `NumericUpDown` editor's spinner buttons and Up/Down keys. |
| `ItemDisplaySelector` | `Func<object, string> ItemDisplaySelector { get; set; }` | Maps a `ItemsSelector` choice to its display text in the popup list; `null` falls back to `ToString()`. It also shapes the closed cell's text for the `ListBox` and `CheckedListBox` kinds, so writing it drops the cached display text. |
| `ItemsSelector` | `Func<object, IReadOnlyList<object>> ItemsSelector { get; set; }` | Maps a row item to the choices a `ComboBox` cell offers while editing. Return a cached list — required (with `ValueSetter`) for the cell to enter edit mode. |
| `KeepImageAspectRatio` | `bool KeepImageAspectRatio { get; set; }` | Whether an icon drawn into an explicit `ImageSize` keeps its aspect ratio, letterboxed inside that box rather than stretched. Defaults to `true`. |
| `Kind` | `DataGridViewColumnKind Kind { get; set; }` | How this column renders and reacts to clicks. Defaults to `Text`. |
| `Mask` | `string Mask { get; set; }` | The input mask a `MaskedText` editor forces — the `Mask` language; empty hosts a plain masked box. |
| `MaxImageSize` | `int MaxImageSize { get; set; }` | The largest edge, in pixels, of one icon in a `MultiImage` cell, or `0` (the default) to fill the row height. Icons stay square. |
| `MaxTime` | `TimeSpan MaxTime { get; set; }` | The latest time the `TimePicker` editor accepts. |
| `Maximum` | `decimal Maximum { get; set; }` | The highest value the `NumericUpDown` editor accepts. |
| `MinTime` | `TimeSpan MinTime { get; set; }` | The earliest time the `TimePicker` editor accepts. |
| `MinimumWidth` | `int MinimumWidth { get; set; }` | The narrowest width the column accepts, floored at 2 px: the lower bound of a user's divider drag and of the share a `Fill` column receives. |
| `Minimum` | `decimal Minimum { get; set; }` | The lowest value the `NumericUpDown` editor accepts. |
| `NumberSelector` | `Func<object, decimal> NumberSelector { get; set; }` | Maps a row item to the number a `NumericUpDown` editor starts from. |
| `NumberSetter` | `Action<object, decimal> NumberSetter { get; set; }` | Writes a committed `NumericUpDown` edit back to the row item, already clamped into [`Minimum`, `Maximum`]. |
| `OverlayImagesSelector` | `Func<object, IReadOnlyList<IImage>> OverlayImagesSelector { get; set; }` | Optional badge icons drawn over the cell's `ImageSelector` icon — the "shortcut arrow / shared / offline" overlays a file list stacks on one item. The selector returns only the badges that currently apply, so several conditions compose; they are drawn at the icon's bottom right, most recent last, each shifted left by one badge width. |
| `OverlaySize` | `int OverlaySize { get; set; }` | The edge, in pixels, of one `OverlayImagesSelector` badge, or `0` (the default) for half the host icon. |
| `ProgressSelector` | `Func<object, int> ProgressSelector { get; set; }` | Maps a row item to the 0..100 fill of a `Progress` cell; values outside the range are clamped. |
| `ReadOnlyCellSelector` | `Func<object, bool> ReadOnlyCellSelector { get; set; }` | Optional per-cell read-only predicate over the row item; `null` means not read-only at the cell level. |
| `ReadOnly` | `bool ReadOnly { get; set; }` | Whether every cell in this column refuses edits and check toggling. Combined with the grid and per-cell levels by `IsCellReadOnly`. |
| `Resizable` | `DataGridViewTriState Resizable { get; set; }` | Whether the user may drag this column's divider: `True` and `False` override the grid's `AllowUserToResizeColumns`; `NotSet` (the default) inherits it — WinForms semantics. |
| `SelectionMode` | `SelectionMode SelectionMode { get; set; }` | How a `ListBox` cell's popup lets the user pick: `One` (the default) is a single pick committed through `ValueSetter`; `MultiSimple` and `MultiExtended` turn the cell into a set-valued one — read through `CheckedItemsSelector`, committed through `CheckedItemsSetter` — and `None` makes it display-only. Ignored by every other kind (a `CheckedListBox` cell is always set-valued). |
| `ShowSeconds` | `bool ShowSeconds { get; set; }` | Whether the `TimePicker` editor carries a seconds part. |
| `SortComparison` | `Comparison<object> SortComparison { get; set; }` | Optional row-item comparison used when this column sorts; `null` falls back to comparing the values `ValueSelector` produces. |
| `SortMode` | `DataGridViewColumnSortMode SortMode { get; set; }` | Whether clicking this column's header sorts the grid. Defaults to `NotSortable`. |
| `TextImageRelation` | `TextImageRelation TextImageRelation { get; set; }` | Where the `ImageSelector` icon sits relative to the cell text. Defaults to `ImageBeforeText`, the classic leading icon. |

| `TimeSelector` | `Func<object, TimeSpan> TimeSelector { get; set; }` | Maps a row item to the time of day a `TimePicker` editor starts from. |
| `TimeSetter` | `Action<object, TimeSpan> TimeSetter { get; set; }` | Writes a committed `TimePicker` edit back to the row item, already clamped into [`MinTime`, `MaxTime`]. |
| `TooltipSelector` | `Func<object, string> TooltipSelector { get; set; }` | Optional per-cell tooltip text, surfaced through `GetCellTooltip`; `null` for none. |
| `Use24HourClock` | `bool Use24HourClock { get; set; }` | Whether the `TimePicker` editor runs a 24-hour clock rather than a 12-hour one with an AM/PM part. |
| `ValueSelector` | `Func<object, object> ValueSelector { get; set; }` | Maps a row item to the value shown in this cell (rendered via `ToString()`). |
| `ValueSetter` | `Action<object, object> ValueSetter { get; set; }` | Writes the choice picked in a `ComboBox` editor back to the row item (row item, chosen value). |
