#### `DataGridViewColumnKind`

How a `DataGridViewColumn` renders its cells. One column class serves every kind — the kind only picks the painter and the click behavior, so the paint path stays a single allocation-free switch instead of a per-type class hierarchy.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Text` | `0` | Plain text from `ValueSelector`, with an optional icon before the text when `ImageSelector` is set. |
| `Check` | `1` | A themed check glyph driven by `CheckedSelector`; clicking toggles through `CheckedSetter` unless the cell is read-only. |
| `Button` | `2` | A themed button face with per-cell text; `EnabledSelector` greys the text and suppresses the content-click event. |
| `Link` | `3` | Accent-colored, underlined text that raises `CellContentClick` on click. |
| `MultiImage` | `4` | Several icons side by side from `ImagesSelector`; each icon is hit-tested individually and reported via `ContentIndex`. |
| `Progress` | `5` | A themed progress fill (0..100) driven by `ProgressSelector`. |
| `ComboBox` | `6` | Text with a drop arrow; editing opens a popup list of the choices from `ItemsSelector` and commits the picked one through `ValueSetter`. |
| `NumericUpDown` | `7` | Plain text whose editor is a hosted `NumericUpDown` bound through `NumberSelector`/`NumberSetter`, clamped and stepped by the column's `Minimum`, `Maximum`, `Increment` and `DecimalPlaces`. |
| `DateTime` | `8` | The formatted date as plain text; editing opens the popup month calendar (the same engine as `DateTimePicker`) and commits the picked day through `DateSetter`, keeping the time of day. |
| `MaskedText` | `9` | Plain text whose editor is a hosted `MaskedTextBox` forcing the column's `Mask`; the masked rendering commits through `TextSetter`. |
| `DomainUpDown` | `10` | Plain text whose editor is a hosted `DomainUpDown` stepping through the choices from `ItemsSelector`; the picked choice commits through `ValueSetter`. |
| `Color` | `11` | A color swatch from `ColorSelector`; editing opens the platform's native color dialog and commits the picked color through `ColorSetter`. |
| `ListBox` | `12` | Text with a drop arrow; editing opens a taller, scrollable popup list of the choices from `ItemsSelector`. Under `One` (the default) the cell shows the single value from `ValueSelector` and a click commits the picked one through `ValueSetter`; under the multi-select modes the cell shows the comma-joined summary of `CheckedItemsSelector` and commits the whole picked set through `CheckedItemsSetter`. |
| `CheckedListBox` | `13` | A set-valued cell: it shows the comma-joined summary of the items `CheckedItemsSelector` yields, and editing opens a popup checked list over `ItemsSelector` whose ticks commit as a whole set through `CheckedItemsSetter`. Every tick is announced through the vetoable `CellItemCheck` event. |
| `TimePicker` | `14` | The formatted time of day as plain text; editing hosts a `TimePicker` over the cell, seeded from `TimeSelector` and committed through `TimeSetter`, clamped by the column's `MinTime` and `MaxTime`. |

#### `DataGridViewColumnSortMode`

Whether and how a `DataGridViewColumn` participates in sorting.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NotSortable` | `0` | Clicking the header does nothing. The default. |
| `Automatic` | `1` | Clicking the header toggles ascending/descending, ordering rows by `SortComparison` when set, otherwise by comparing the values the column's `ValueSelector` produces. |

#### `DataGridViewEditMode`

How a `DataGridView` cell enters edit mode — the Windows Forms modes the toolkit's focus model can honor.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EditOnKeystrokeOrF2` | `0` | Typing a character, F2 on the current cell or a double-click begins the edit. The default. |
| `EditOnEnter` | `1` | A cell begins editing as soon as it becomes current — clicking it, or Tab/Enter moving there from a committed edit; the keystroke gestures keep working. |
| `EditProgrammatically` | `2` | Only an explicit `BeginEdit` call begins an edit; every user gesture is ignored. |

#### `DataGridViewTriState`

A boolean that can also defer to a grid-level default, like its Windows Forms namesake — `Resizable` uses it to override (or inherit) `AllowUserToResizeColumns` per column.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NotSet` | `0` | Defer to the grid's setting. The default. |
| `True` | `1` | Explicitly enabled, regardless of the grid. |
| `False` | `2` | Explicitly disabled, regardless of the grid. |

| `Start` | `DateTime Start { get; }` | The first selected day. |

#### `DateTimePicker`

A date field in the ComboBox shape: a closed, owner-drawn field showing `Value` in the invariant `Format` with a themed drop arrow, which opens a light-dismiss popup hosting the same month page as `MonthCalendar` — both surfaces run one shared engine, so they stay pixel- and behavior-identical. Clicking a day commits it into `Value` preserving the time of day; Escape or clicking elsewhere cancels. With `ShowCheckBox` the field carries a check box; while unchecked the text greys and the value cannot be changed. Closed, Up/Down step the day (the classic control steps whichever date part is focused — per-part focus is not implemented yet, and neither is time editing) and Alt+Down or F4 opens the calendar.

Inherits `OwnerDrawnControl`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DateTimePicker` | `DateTimePicker()` |  |
| `Checked` | `bool Checked { get; set; }` | Whether the value applies. While `ShowCheckBox` is on and this is off, the text greys and every value-changing gesture is suppressed. |
| `CustomFormat` | `string CustomFormat { get; set; }` | The invariant pattern used while `Format` is `Custom`; empty renders an empty field. |
| `DateSelectable` | `Func<DateTime, bool> DateSelectable { get; set; }` | An optional predicate that blocks individual days in the drop-down from being picked, on top of `MinDate`/`MaxDate`. |
| `DayBackgroundProvider` | `Func<DateTime, Color?> DayBackgroundProvider { get; set; }` | An optional per-day background colour for the drop-down calendar — shade holidays and the like. Applied the next time the calendar opens. |
| `DayTooltipProvider` | `Func<DateTime, string> DayTooltipProvider { get; set; }` | An optional per-day tooltip for the drop-down calendar, shown on hover. |
| `DroppedDown` | `bool DroppedDown { get; }` | Whether the calendar popup is currently open. |
| `Focusable` | `protected override bool Focusable { get; }` |  |
| `Format` | `DateTimePickerFormat Format { get; set; }` | How the closed field renders `Value`; always the invariant culture. |
| `MaxDate` | `DateTime MaxDate { get; set; }` | The latest pickable date; assignments and steps clamp to it. |

#### `DockContent`

A titled, dockable pane hosted by a `DockPanel` (§7.2). It is an ordinary container — its `Controls` hold real nested children that realize as native peers — with a caption bar (title, optional `ImageIndex` icon and close/float/auto-hide buttons) that the owning `DockPanel` paints just above the content, plus a `DockState` that says whether it is docked to an edge, in the central document well, floating in its own window, or collapsed to an auto-hide strip.

Inherits `Panel`.

| --- | --- | --- |

| `AllowClose` | `bool AllowClose { get; set; }` | Whether the caption shows a close button. |
| `AllowFloat` | `bool AllowFloat { get; set; }` | Whether the caption shows a float button and the pane may be torn off into a window. |
| `DockEdge` | `DockEdge DockEdge { get; set; }` | The edge a docked or auto-hidden pane clings to. Changing it re-docks the pane when it is currently on an edge. |

| `DockState` | `DockState DockState { get; set; }` | Where this pane currently lives. Read freely; assign to move it (the owning `DockPanel` performs the move so the layout stays consistent). Before a manager owns the pane the setter only records the wish. |
| `ImageIndex` | `int ImageIndex { get; set; }` | The index into the owning `ImageList` of the caption/tab icon, or -1 for none. |

The edge a docked or auto-hidden `DockContent` clings to.

| `Top` | `1` | The top edge. |
| `Right` | `2` | The right edge. |

#### `DockGuide`

A directional docking target offered by the drag overlay. The four edges split the region the pointer is over (or the whole panel, for the outer guides); `Center` drops the pane into the hovered group as a new tab.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `None` | `0` | No guide is under the pointer. |
| `Left` | `1` | Dock to the left of the hovered region. |
| `Top` | `2` | Dock above the hovered region. |
| `Right` | `3` | Dock to the right of the hovered region. |
| `Bottom` | `4` | Dock below the hovered region. |
| `Center` | `5` | Drop into the hovered group as a new tab. |
| `PanelLeft` | `6` | Dock against the panel's own left edge, spanning its full height. |
| `PanelTop` | `7` | Dock against the panel's own top edge, spanning its full width. |
| `PanelRight` | `8` | Dock against the panel's own right edge, spanning its full height. |
| `PanelBottom` | `9` | Dock against the panel's own bottom edge, spanning its full width. |

#### `DockPanel`

A Visual-Studio-style docking manager (§7.2): a container that hosts movable `DockContent` panes around a central document tab well. It owns the layout tree — nested splitter regions whose leaves are tab groups — and paints every caption bar, tab strip, splitter and auto-hide edge strip itself in the native theme, so the whole arrangement is drawn and hit-tested in one place. Panes can be docked to an edge, tabbed together, split apart with draggable splitters, torn off into floating windows, or collapsed to auto-hide strips that fly out on hover; dragging a caption raises docking overlay guides with a translucent landing preview. The arrangement round-trips through `SaveLayout`/`LoadLayout`.

Inherits `OwnerDrawnControl`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DockPanel` | `DockPanel()` | Creates an empty docking manager. |
| `ActiveContent` | `DockContent ActiveContent { get; }` | The pane with the active caption, or `null` when the panel is empty. |
| `Contents` | `IReadOnlyList<DockContent> Contents { get; }` | Every pane the manager owns, in the order they were added. |
| `DocumentTabStripEdge` | `TabAlignment DocumentTabStripEdge { get; set; }` | Which edge each tab group's document-tab strip sits on. `Top` and `Bottom` lay the tabs out in a horizontal row (bottom by default, the classic document well); `Left`/`Right` stack them in a vertical strip whose width fits the widest caption. |
| `Focusable` | `protected override bool Focusable { get; }` |  |
| `ImageList` | `ImageList ImageList { get; set; }` | The icons `ImageIndex` indexes into, or `null`. |
| `ShowDocumentCaption` | `bool ShowDocumentCaption { get; set; }` | Whether the document area carries a caption bar of its own. Default `true`. |
| `AddDocument` | `void AddDocument(DockContent content)` | Adds a pane to the central document well. |
| `Add` | `void Add(DockContent content, DockState state = 2, DockEdge edge = 0)` | Adds a pane to the manager in the given state. A `Docked` or `AutoHide` pane clings to `edge`; a `Document` pane joins the central well. |
| `DockToEdge` | `void DockToEdge(DockContent content, DockEdge edge)` | Docks a pane to one of the four edges, joining any existing group on that edge. |
| `IsInputKey` | `protected override bool IsInputKey(Keys keyData)` |  |
| `LoadLayout` | `void LoadLayout(string layout, Func<string, DockContent> resolve)` | Restores an arrangement previously produced by `SaveLayout`. `resolve` maps a pane's persistence key back to the live `DockContent`; a key it cannot resolve is skipped. |
| `OnKeyDown` | `protected override void OnKeyDown(KeyEventArgs e)` |  |
| `OnMouseDown` | `protected override void OnMouseDown(MouseEventArgs e)` |  |
| `OnMouseLeave` | `protected override void OnMouseLeave(EventArgs e)` |  |
| `OnMouseMove` | `protected override void OnMouseMove(MouseEventArgs e)` |  |
| `OnMouseUp` | `protected override void OnMouseUp(MouseEventArgs e)` |  |
| `OnPaint` | `protected override void OnPaint(PaintEventArgs e)` |  |
| `SaveLayout` | `string SaveLayout()` | Serialises the whole arrangement — the split tree, every pane's state, edge, active flag and floating-window bounds — to a compact, reflection-free string. |
| `ActiveContentChanged` | `event EventHandler ActiveContentChanged` | Raised after `ActiveContent` changes. |

#### `DockState`

Where a `DockContent` lives inside its owning `DockPanel` — the Visual-Studio docking states. The edge a docked or auto-hidden pane clings to is carried separately by `DockEdge`.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Hidden` | `0` | Not shown anywhere: no caption, no tab, no edge strip. The pane keeps its children but their peers are vetoed, so it costs nothing until it is shown again. |
| `Docked` | `1` | Pinned to one of the four edges (see `DockEdge`), sharing a tab well with any siblings docked to the same region and separated from the rest by a draggable splitter. |
| `Document` | `2` | In the central document tab well — the editor area a VS-style shell fills with open files. Several documents share one tab strip. |
| `Floating` | `3` | In its own top-level window, draggable and independent of the panel. |
| `AutoHide` | `4` | Collapsed to a labelled strip on its edge; hovering or clicking the strip flies the pane out over the content, and it slides back when focus leaves. |

#### `DockStyle`

The container edge a control glues itself to (see `Dock`). Docked siblings claim their edges of the container's `DisplayRectangle` in `Controls` order, each shrinking the rectangle left for the next; `Fill` takes whatever remains. Docking and anchoring are mutually exclusive — the property assigned last wins, exactly like Windows Forms.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `None` | `0` | Not docked; the control is positioned by `Bounds` and `Anchor`. |
| `Top` | `1` | Glued to the top edge, spanning the available width; the control keeps its height. |
| `Bottom` | `2` | Glued to the bottom edge, spanning the available width; the control keeps its height. |
| `Left` | `3` | Glued to the left edge, spanning the available height; the control keeps its width. |
| `Right` | `4` | Glued to the right edge, spanning the available height; the control keeps its width. |
| `Fill` | `5` | Fills the rectangle left over after every edge-docked sibling took its share. |

#### `Expander`

A collapsible container (§7.9): a themed header row — triangle glyph plus `Text` — over a content area of ordinary child controls. Collapsing shrinks the control to the header row, remembers the expanded height and hides the child peers; the children's own visibility flags stay untouched, so expanding restores exactly what was there — while collapsed they read `Visible` as `false`, because that getter is effective and the content genuinely is not on screen. A header click or the Space key toggles.

Inherits `OwnerDrawnControl`.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `Expander` | `Expander()` |  |

| `Focusable` | `protected override bool Focusable { get; }` |  |

Defaults to `false` (the plain triangle). |

The chain sees keys from owner-drawn surfaces; a focused native text widget consumes its keys inside the widget, where no preview exists yet. |

Returns `DialogResult` — `Cancel` when the form was closed without a verdict (close box, Alt+F4). The form unrealizes on return and can be shown again. |
| `Show` | `void Show()` | Shows this form modelessly on the running application's backend: the form realizes, appears, and the call returns immediately — the window then lives on the already-pumping message loop and closes through the usual `FormClosing`/`FormClosed` path. #### `FormBorderStyle`

The frame a `Form`'s native window wears. Win32 maps each value to window-style bits (`WS_THICKFRAME`, `WS_CAPTION`, `WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW` …) toggled live on the HWND; GTK maps to `gtk_window_set_resizable`/`set_decorated`/`set_type_hint`, where the window manager has the final say over the exact frame.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `None` | `0` | No frame at all — no caption, no border, not resizable. |
| `FixedSingle` | `1` | A caption with a thin single-line border; not resizable by the user. |
| `FixedDialog` | `2` | A dialog frame; not resizable by the user. |
| `FixedToolWindow` | `3` | A tool-window caption (small, no taskbar entry on Windows); not resizable. |
| `Sizable` | `4` | The standard resizable window frame. The default. |

#### `ImageList`

Backend-independent icon storage shared by list, tree, combo and toolbar controls. Images are added as raw 32-bit ARGB pixels long before any backend exists — typically while a form is being constructed — and are materialized into native `IImage`s lazily, the first time a realized control paints them. All images share one fixed `ImageSize`, exactly like its Windows Forms namesake.

Implements `IDisposable`.

| --- | --- | --- |

| `ImageList` | `ImageList(int edgeLength)` | Creates a list of square `edgeLength`-pixel images. |
| `Count` | `int Count { get; }` | The number of images stored. |
| `ImageSize` | `Size ImageSize { get; }` | The fixed pixel size every image in this list has. |
| `AddBadged` | `int AddBadged(int baseIndex, ReadOnlySpan<int> badgeArgb, int badgeWidth, int badgeHeight, ContentAlignment corner = 8)` | Adds a copy of the image at `baseIndex` with a badge composed onto it — small status overlays like "modified" or "locked" — and returns the new entry's index. The badge pixels (row-major 32-bit ARGB, `badgeWidth`×`badgeHeight`) are blended over the base with a straight alpha-over: opaque badge pixels overwrite, fully transparent ones preserve the base. `corner` anchors the badge within the image, bottom-right by default. The base entry stays untouched. |
| `AddIco` | `int AddIco(ReadOnlySpan<byte> ico)` | Adds an image from encoded ICO bytes, letting the decoder pick the entry closest to `ImageSize`, and returns its index. A decoded size other than `ImageSize` is resampled to fit with nearest-neighbor scaling. |
| `AddIco` | `int AddIco(string key, ReadOnlySpan<byte> ico)` | Adds a decoded ICO under a lookup `key`; see `AddIco`. |
| `AddPng` | `int AddPng(ReadOnlySpan<byte> png)` | Adds an image from encoded PNG bytes (the `ImageDecoder` subset: 8-bit non-interlaced grayscale/RGB/RGBA/palette) and returns its index. A decoded size other than `ImageSize` is resampled to fit with nearest-neighbor scaling — crisp for the icon-sized art this list holds, no filtering. |
| `AddPng` | `int AddPng(string key, ReadOnlySpan<byte> png)` | Adds a decoded PNG under a lookup `key`; see `AddPng`. |
| `Add` | `int Add(AnimatedImage image)` | Adds a still or animated `AnimatedImage` as an entry and returns its index — the same collection interface, so any control that draws from an image list (tree, list, tab, tool strip …) can carry an animated icon. The list registers an animated entry with the shared `AnimationClock` and raises `FrameChanged` as it advances; each frame is realized against the drawing backend and scaled into the icon slot exactly like a still entry. |
| `Add` | `int Add(ReadOnlySpan<int> argb)` | Adds an image from row-major 32-bit ARGB pixels and returns its index. |
| `Add` | `int Add(string key, AnimatedImage image)` | Adds an `AnimatedImage` under a lookup `key`. |

| `Dispose` | `void Dispose()` | Disposes all realized native bitmaps; the pixel data stays usable. |
| `IndexOfKey` | `int IndexOfKey(string key)` | The index of the image stored under `key`, or `-1` when the key is empty or unknown. Keys are matched case-insensitively, exactly like the Windows Forms namesake. |
| `FrameChanged` | `event EventHandler FrameChanged` | Raised as any animated entry's frame advances, so every control drawing from this list can repaint. A control subscribes when the list is assigned and unsubscribes when it is replaced; the list keeps the shared `AnimationClock` ticking while it holds an animated entry. |

#### `Label`

A non-interactive line of static text, backed by the platform's native label widget. Supports WinForms-style `AutoSize`, `TextAlign`, `BorderStyle`, mnemonic rendering (`UseMnemonic`) and an `Image` beside the caption.

Inherits `OwnerDrawnControl`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Label` | `Label()` |  |
| `AutoSize` | `bool AutoSize { get; set; }` | When `true`, the label sizes itself to fit its content in the theme's default font. The size is computed through the backend's text measurement on realization and again on every `Text` change; before realization the wish is simply buffered. Defaults to `false`, matching Windows Forms. |
| `BorderStyle` | `BorderStyle BorderStyle { get; set; }` | The border drawn around the label — `None` or `FixedSingle`. Rendered natively on Win32 (`WS_BORDER`); GTK has no native label frame, so the value is not rendered there. A painted label draws it from the theme on every backend. |
| `Focusable` | `protected override bool Focusable { get; }` | Static text never takes keyboard focus (and so never joins the tab order). |
| `ImageAlign` | `ContentAlignment ImageAlign { get; set; }` | Where the image anchors within the label's bounds when it is the only content — a caption-less label places its image by this rather than by `TextAlign`, matching Windows Forms. Defaults to `MiddleCenter`. |
| `Image` | `IImage Image { get; set; }` | The image shown beside the caption, or `null`. Assigning one moves the label off the platform's static widget and onto the painter, because no platform static renders a bitmap and a caption together; clearing it moves the label back. The swap is invisible to the application — every property keeps its value across it. |
| `IsNativeWidget` | `override bool IsNativeWidget { get; }` | Whether this label is currently rendered by a real platform widget. |
| `TextAlign` | `ContentAlignment TextAlign { get; set; }` | Where the text sits within the label's bounds. Win32 static controls honor the horizontal component plus a coarse vertical centering only; GTK honors all nine anchors. A label carrying an image is painted, and honors all nine everywhere. |
| `TextImageRelation` | `TextImageRelation TextImageRelation { get; set; }` | How the image sits relative to the caption. Defaults to `ImageBeforeText` — the icon leads, the caption follows. |
| `UseMnemonic` | `bool UseMnemonic { get; set; }` | Whether `&` in `Text` marks the following character as a mnemonic and renders it underlined (`&&` escapes a literal ampersand). Alt+mnemonic focuses the next tab stop after the label through the owning form's dialog-key chain — fed by owner-drawn surfaces; keys held inside native widgets cannot trigger it yet. Defaults to `true`. |
| `OnPaint` | `protected override void OnPaint(PaintEventArgs e)` |  |
| `OnTextChanged` | `protected override void OnTextChanged(EventArgs e)` |  |

Describes a label edit at both ends of its life. For `BeforeLabelEdit` it carries the item's current text and `CancelEdit` vetoes the edit before it starts; for `AfterLabelEdit` it carries the entered text and `CancelEdit` discards it, leaving the item's original text in place.

Inherits `EventArgs`.

For `BeforeLabelEdit` it carries the item's current text and `CancelEdit` vetoes the edit before it starts; for `AfterLabelEdit` it carries the entered text and `CancelEdit` discards it, leaving the item's original text in place. |
| `CancelEdit` | `bool CancelEdit { get; set; }` | Set by a handler to veto the pending edit (before) or discard the entered text (after). |
| `Item` | `int Item { get; }` | The index of the edited item. |
| `Label` | `string Label { get; }` | The label text: the current text before an edit, the text the user entered after one — or `null` when the edit was cancelled. |

#### `ListView`

An owner-drawn list view painted in the native theme, covering the full `ListViewView` family: `Details` (multi-column grid with a header row), `List` (single vertical column), `LargeIcon`/`SmallIcon` (cells flowing left-to-right in rows) and `Tile` (icon beside a two-line text block). Items can carry check boxes (`CheckBoxes`, vetoable through `ItemCheck`), group into titled sections (`Groups`/`ShowGroups`), sort in place (`Sorting`/`ItemSorter`/`Sort`, with `ColumnClick` on the Details header) and edit their labels through a hosted native text box (`LabelEdit`/`BeginEdit`). Selection follows the classic control: `MultiSelect` (default) gives the extended Ctrl/Shift model with sorted `SelectedIndices` and one `SelectedIndexChanged` per gesture. Painting is virtualized to the visible row window in every view, so it stays cheap for very large `Items` collections.

Inherits `OwnerDrawnControl`.

#### `MaskedTextBox`

A `TextBox` whose content is forced through an input mask — phone numbers, dates, license keys. The mask engine lives entirely in the core: the control uses the plain native text widget of every backend, maps every candidate value into the mask's slots and pushes the rendered result — and the caret that belongs with it — back to the widget.

Inherits `TextBox`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MaskedTextBox` | `MaskedTextBox()` |  |

| `Mask` | `string Mask { get; set; }` | The input mask. Setting it re-maps the current content into the new mask; content that no longer fits is discarded and the box falls back to the empty rendering (all prompts). An empty mask turns the box back into a plain `TextBox`. |
| `PromptChar` | `char PromptChar { get; set; }` | The character rendered in unfilled slots. Changing it re-renders the current content; slot values equal to the old prompt read as empty and therefore adopt the new prompt. |
| `GetTextWithoutPromptOrLiterals` | `string GetTextWithoutPromptOrLiterals()` | Returns only the characters the user actually entered — mask literals and prompt characters stripped. Without a mask this is simply `Text`. |
| `OnMaskInputRejected` | `protected virtual void OnMaskInputRejected(MaskInputRejectedEventArgs e)` | Raises `MaskInputRejected`. |

#### `MenuStrip`

The application menu bar: a horizontal, owner-drawn row of top-level items whose drop-downs open through the shared `MenuDropDown` engine — icons, check marks, shortcut text, cascading submenus and light dismiss included. #### `MonthCalendar`

An owner-drawn one-month calendar page in the native theme: a title row ("July 2026", invariant) with previous/next paging arrows, a day-of-week header of two-letter invariant names starting at `FirstDayOfWeek`, and a 6×7 day grid with leading/trailing days greyed and today circled in the accent color. A click selects one day; Shift+click or dragging selects a range of up to `MaxSelectionCount` days. The keyboard moves a focus day (arrows), pages months (PageUp/PageDown, with Ctrl whole years), jumps to the month edges (Home/End) and selects (Enter/Space); the wheel pages months. Days outside [`MinDate`, `MaxDate`] paint disabled and reject clicks. Bolded dates are not implemented yet.

#### `NativeFormsSynchronizationContext`

The `SynchronizationContext``Run` installs on the UI thread for the duration of the message loop: `Post` queues onto the loop through the backend (like `BeginInvoke`), `Send` runs inline on the loop thread and blocks — propagating exceptions — from any other (like `Invoke`). This is what makes `await` continuations inside event handlers resume on the UI thread.

#### `OwnerDrawnControl`

Base class for controls the toolkit paints itself (everything the platform has no native widget for, plus anything we want pixel-identical across platforms). It realizes onto a single `ICanvasPeer` and turns that surface's paint and input events into the familiar `OnPaint`/`OnMouseDown`/… overrides. A subclass draws through `Graphics` using `Theme` so it matches the host desktop.

#### `PictureBoxSizeMode`

How a `PictureBox` fits its image into the client area, matching the semantics of `System.Windows.Forms.PictureBoxSizeMode`.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Normal` | `0` | The image sits in the top-left corner at native size and is clipped if larger. |
| `StretchImage` | `1` | The image is stretched to fill the client area, ignoring its aspect ratio. |
| `CenterImage` | `2` | The image is centered at native size and is clipped if larger. |
| `Zoom` | `3` | The image is scaled to the largest size that fits, keeping its aspect ratio. |
| `FitToWidth` | `4` | The image is scaled so its width fills the client area, keeping its aspect ratio, and is centered vertically — the height then over- or under-fills and is clipped to the client area. |
| `FitToHeight` | `5` | The image is scaled so its height fills the client area, keeping its aspect ratio, and is centered horizontally — the width then over- or under-fills and is clipped to the client area. |

#### `Ribbon`

An Office-style ribbon (§7.9): a strip of `RibbonTab`s across the top, each showing its `RibbonGroup`s side by side — every group a framed box with its caption running along the bottom edge. Items come in two sizes: `Large` (big icon over the caption, full group height) and `Small` (small icon beside the caption, three stacked per column), and that stacking is what makes a ribbon read as a ribbon. Groups that no longer fit collapse into a single drop-down button, and `Minimized` folds the group area away entirely, leaving the tabs.

Inherits `OwnerDrawnControl`.

Minimizing already shrinks the control to it and raises `PreferredHeightChanged`; this getter lets a host read the target directly. |

#### `TableLayoutPanel`

A `Panel` that slices its client area into a `ColumnCount` × `RowCount` grid and fills each child into its cell minus the child's `Margin`. Tracks are sized by `ColumnStyles`/`RowStyles` (absolute pixels, auto-sized to the largest child, or a percent share of what is left); unstyled tracks share the remaining space equally. Children without an explicit `SetCellPosition` auto-place row-major into free cells, spans stretch across neighboring tracks, and `CellBorderStyle` paints the themed grid. Layout runs in logical space, so `AutoScroll` scrolls an overflowing grid.

Inherits `Panel`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |

| `ColumnStyles` | `TableLayoutStyleCollection<ColumnStyle> ColumnStyles { get; }` | The sizing rules per column, in track order. |
| `RowCount` | `int RowCount { get; set; }` | The number of rows; at least one. |
| `RowStyles` | `TableLayoutStyleCollection<RowStyle> RowStyles { get; }` | The sizing rules per row, in track order. |
| `GetCellPosition` | `TableLayoutPanelCellPosition GetCellPosition(Control control)` | The cell a control was pinned to, or (-1, -1) while it auto-places. |
| `GetColumnSpan` | `int GetColumnSpan(Control control)` | The number of columns the control spans; 1 by default. |
| `GetRowSpan` | `int GetRowSpan(Control control)` | The number of rows the control spans; 1 by default. |
| `OnPaint` | `protected override void OnPaint(PaintEventArgs e)` |  |
| `SetCellPosition` | `void SetCellPosition(Control control, int column, int row)` | Pins a control to the given cell; auto-placement flows the other children around it. |
| `SetColumnSpan` | `void SetColumnSpan(Control control, int value)` | Stretches a control across the given number of columns. |
| `SetRowSpan` | `void SetRowSpan(Control control, int value)` | Stretches a control across the given number of rows. |

#### `Timer`

A recurring timer whose `Tick` fires on the UI thread, driven by the platform message loop — the moral equivalent of `System.Windows.Forms.Timer`. Marquee progress, caret blink, tooltip delays and key autorepeat are all built on it.

Inherits `Component`. Implements `IDisposable`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Timer` | `Timer()` | Creates a timer bound to whatever backend the application runs on. |
| `Enabled` | `bool Enabled { get; set; }` | Whether the timer is ticking. Setting the same value again is a no-op. |
| `Interval` | `int Interval { get; set; }` | The tick period in milliseconds. Setting it while the timer runs restarts the period. |
| `Dispose` | `protected override void Dispose(bool disposing)` | Stops the timer and releases the native timer source. |
| `Start` | `void Start()` | Starts the timer; identical to setting `Enabled` to `true`. |
| `Stop` | `void Stop()` | Stops the timer; identical to setting `Enabled` to `false`. |
| `Tick` | `event EventHandler Tick` | Raised on the UI thread every `Interval` milliseconds while `Enabled`. |

#### `Toast`

Shows transient in-app notifications — small `InfoBar`s anchored to the bottom-right of a form that fade in, stack upward when several are live at once, and fade out while sliding down when they expire or are dismissed. The in-window counterpart of the OS tray balloon, for "Saved", "Update available" and the like.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Show` | `static void Show(Form form, string title, string message, InfoBarSeverity severity = 0, int durationMs = 3000)` | Pops a toast on `form` with the given text and severity; it stacks above any live toasts and removes itself after `durationMs` milliseconds or when dismissed. |

#### `ToggleSwitch`

An owner-drawn on/off switch — the modern `CheckBox` alternative: a pill-shaped track (accent-filled while on, border-grey while off) with a themed thumb that sits left for off and right for on, and an optional caption beside it. Toggles on click or Space and raises `CheckedChanged`. The thumb snaps to its new side; there is no slide animation.

#### `TokenBox`

A tag / chip input: a text field whose committed entries become removable chips. Enter or a comma turns the typed text into a chip; each chip carries an × zone that deletes it and Backspace on the empty editor removes the last one. An optional `AutoCompleteSource` delegate drops down a filtered suggestion list under the editor. The chips flow left-to-right and wrap; a hosted native `TextBox` holds the caret so typing, selection and clipboard stay platform-native. Used for tags, recipient fields and search scopes.

Inherits `OwnerDrawnControl`.

| `ChipStyleProvider` | `Func<string, TokenChipStyle> ChipStyleProvider { get; set; }` | An optional per-chip style (fill, text colour, font style) chosen from the token text, so a host can colour-code chips or italicise/bolden them. `null` uses the accent-tinted default. |
| `Focusable` | `protected override bool Focusable { get; }` |  |
| `PlaceholderText` | `string PlaceholderText { get; set; }` | The greyed hint shown while the field is empty. |

| `IsInputKey` | `protected override bool IsInputKey(Keys keyData)` | Enter and comma commit a chip, so they stay out of the form's AcceptButton routing. |
| `OnMouseDown` | `protected override void OnMouseDown(MouseEventArgs e)` |  |

#### `ToolStripDropDownItem`

A strip item that can carry a drop-down of child items: the shared base of `ToolStripMenuItem`, `ToolStripDropDownButton` and `ToolStripSplitButton`, mirroring the Windows Forms hierarchy. The child collection bubbles its changes through this item so the hosting strip repaints (and an open drop-down refreshes) no matter how deep the change happened.

Inherits `ToolStripItem`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ToolStripDropDownItem` | `protected ToolStripDropDownItem()` |  |

#### `ToolStripItem`

Base class for everything hosted by a strip — menu items, toolbar buttons, separators, status labels. An item is not a `Control`: it owns no peer and no bounds of its own; the hosting strip (or the drop-down engine) lays it out and paints it. State changes bubble to the owning collection so the strip repaints without the item ever knowing who displays it.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ToolStripItem` | `protected ToolStripItem()` |  |
| `Command` | `ICommand Command { get; set; }` | The MVVM command this item invokes. `PerformClick` executes it, its `CanExecuteChanged` re-evaluates `Enabled`, and the hosting strip repaints — the same wiring a bound button gets. |
| `Enabled` | `bool Enabled { get; set; }` | Whether the item reacts to the user. With a `Command` attached the command's `CanExecute` gates the effective value on top of the assigned one, so a view-model guard greys the item out automatically. |
| `ImageIndex` | `int ImageIndex { get; set; }` | The index of this item's icon within `ImageList`; negative for none. |
| `ImageKey` | `string ImageKey { get; set; }` | The key of this item's icon in the owning toolbar's `ImageList`, used when `ImageIndex` is unset (< 0). The index takes precedence when both are set. |
| `ImageList` | `ImageList ImageList { get; set; }` | The icon store `ImageIndex` indexes into, or `null` for none. |
| `Image` | `IImage Image { get; set; }` | A direct icon for the item; wins over `ImageList` + `ImageIndex`. |
| `Tag` | `object Tag { get; set; }` | Arbitrary user data riding along with the item. |
| `Text` | `string Text { get; set; }` | The caption. `&` marks the following character as the mnemonic (`&&` escapes a literal ampersand). |
| `ToolTipText` | `string ToolTipText { get; set; }` | Hover text for this item, the moral equivalent of `ToolStripItem.ToolTipText`. An item owns no peer, so the tip is floated by the hosting `ToolStrip` rather than by the `ToolTip` component, which registers per `Control` — but the delays and the popup painting are the same ones. Empty or `null` means no tip. |
| `Visible` | `bool Visible { get; set; }` | Whether the item occupies space and paints. |
| `OnClick` | `protected virtual void OnClick(EventArgs e)` | Raises `Click`. Subclasses toggle their check state before delegating here. |
| `PerformClick` | `void PerformClick()` | Activates the item as a user click would: raises `Click` and executes `Command`. A no-op while the item is not `Enabled`. |
| `Click` | `event EventHandler Click` | Raised when the item is activated (click, Enter, shortcut). |

The ordered set of items a strip (or a drop-down) hosts. Mutations and item-state changes raise `Changed`, which the hosting strip turns into a repaint — the collection itself never touches a surface, so the same item tree serves menu bars, drop-downs, toolbars and status bars.

| `Add` | `void Add(ToolStripItem item)` | Appends an item. |
| `Clear` | `void Clear()` | Removes all items. |
| `GetEnumerator` | `IEnumerator<ToolStripItem> GetEnumerator()` |  |

#### `ToolTip`

Per-control hover text, the moral equivalent of `System.Windows.Forms.ToolTip`. Register a text per control via `SetToolTip`; when the pointer rests on a control for `InitialDelay` milliseconds a small themed popup appears near the cursor, and it hides again when the pointer leaves, a button goes down, or `AutoPopDelay` elapses.

Inherits `Component`. Implements `IDisposable`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ToolTip` | `ToolTip()` |  |
| `Active` | `bool Active { get; }` | Whether a tip is currently up. For an owner-drawn control this is the toolkit popup's own visibility. For a native widget it means the platform tooltip has been raised for it and not yet taken down — the final say on painting the tip belongs to the platform, so treat this as "a tip was raised" rather than a promise about pixels. |
| `AutoPopDelay` | `int AutoPopDelay { get; set; }` | Milliseconds a visible tip stays up before hiding on its own. Defaults to 5000. |
| `InitialDelay` | `int InitialDelay { get; set; }` | Milliseconds the pointer must rest on a control before its tip appears. Defaults to 500. |
| `Dispose` | `protected override void Dispose(bool disposing)` | Hides the tip, detaches every observed control and releases the native popup and timer. |
| `GetToolTip` | `string GetToolTip(Control control)` | The registered hover text for `control`, or an empty string. |
| `Hide` | `void Hide()` | Hides the tip and stops any pending delay. |
| `SetToolTip` | `void SetToolTip(Control control, string text)` | Registers (or, with an empty text, removes) the hover text for a control. Every control is hooked immediately through `PointerMove`, which every peer feeds — a canvas as well as a widget — so a registration never silently does nothing, and a control that moves between the two halves (PRD §12) keeps its tip across the swap. An owner-drawn surface is hooked for its clicks as well, which is the one channel a canvas has and a widget does not. |

#### `TreeListView`

An owner-drawn TreeView × ListView hybrid painted in the native theme: the first column renders an expandable `TreeNode` hierarchy (indent, expand/collapse glyphs, optional check boxes and per-node icons from an `ImageList`), the remaining columns render per-node text produced by reflection-free `TextSelector`s under a ListView-style header row. Selection is full-row; expand/collapse, checking and keyboard navigation behave exactly like `TreeView`. The expanded part of the tree is flattened into a list of visible rows and painting is virtualized to the rows intersecting the client area, so it stays cheap for very large trees.

#### `TreeView`

An owner-drawn tree view painted in the native theme: hierarchical `TreeNode`s with expand/collapse glyphs, optional connector lines, per-node icons from an `ImageList`, optional check boxes, single selection and wheel/keyboard scrolling. The expanded part of the tree is flattened into a list of visible rows and painting is virtualized to the rows intersecting the client area, so it stays cheap for very large trees.

Inherits `OwnerDrawnControl`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TreeView` | `TreeView()` | Creates a tree view. |
| `AllowReorder` | `bool AllowReorder { get; set; }` | Whether nodes can be dragged within the tree to reorder or reparent them, with a live insertion marker. Off by default. While on, pressing a node and dragging past a few pixels starts a drag (`ItemDrag`); the pointer's position within the target row picks above / onto / below; `NodeDragOver` can reject a target and `NodeDrop` can veto the release. A node is never droppable into its own subtree. This is intra-tree node movement, distinct from the cross-control `AllowDrop` data drag. |
| `AutoExpandDelay` | `int AutoExpandDelay { get; set; }` | How long the pointer must dwell on a collapsed node while dragging before it auto-expands, in milliseconds. Defaults to 700; set to 0 to disable hover-expansion. Only active during a drag. |

#### `ContextMenuRequestedEventArgs`

The native side of a single `Control`. A peer owns one platform widget (an HWND, a GtkWidget*, an NSView …) and exposes only the operations the core needs to keep that widget in sync with the managed control. All coordinates are in the parent's client space, top-left origin, pixels — exactly like Windows Forms.

Inherits `EventArgs`.

All coordinates are in the parent's client space, top-left origin, pixels — exactly like Windows Forms. |

#### `ICanvasPeer`

The native side of an owner-drawn control: a single focusable, paintable surface. Every custom control in the toolkit is realized onto one of these, so a backend implements drawing and input exactly once (in its canvas peer) rather than once per control. The peer raises paint and input events; the managed control responds by drawing through the supplied `IGraphics`. It is also a `IContainerPeer` — owner-drawn containers (panels, group boxes) host native children on top of their painted surface, just like any Windows Forms control can.

Implements `IContainerPeer`, `IControlPeer`, `IDisposable`.

| `SetFocusable` | `void SetFocusable(bool focusable)` | Sets whether the surface can receive keyboard focus. |
| `KeyDown` | `event EventHandler<KeyEventArgs> KeyDown` | Raised when a key goes down while focused. |
| `KeyPress` | `event EventHandler<KeyPressEventArgs> KeyPress` | Raised when a character is typed while focused. |
| `KeyUp` | `event EventHandler<KeyEventArgs> KeyUp` | Raised when a key is released while focused. |
| `MouseDown` | `event EventHandler<MouseEventArgs> MouseDown` | Raised when a mouse button goes down over the surface. |
| `MouseLeave` | `event EventHandler MouseLeave` | Raised when the pointer leaves the surface. |
| `MouseMove` | `event EventHandler<MouseEventArgs> MouseMove` | Raised when the pointer moves over the surface. |
| `MouseUp` | `event EventHandler<MouseEventArgs> MouseUp` | Raised when a mouse button is released. |
| `MouseWheel` | `event EventHandler<MouseEventArgs> MouseWheel` | Raised when the mouse wheel turns over the surface. |
| `Paint` | `event EventHandler<PaintEventArgs> Paint` | Raised when a region needs repainting. |

#### `IControlPeer`

Implements `IDisposable`.

Win32 answers the parent-routed `WM_CTLCOLOR*` messages with the values (classic push buttons ignore them — a documented USER32 limit); GTK overrides the widget's style colors. |
| `SetCursor` | `void SetCursor(Cursor cursor)` | Sets the pointer shape shown over the widget. Win32 resolves it in the `WM_SETCURSOR` handler; GTK sets the GDK window's cursor once that window exists. |
| `SetEnabled` | `void SetEnabled(bool enabled)` | Enables or greys out the widget for user interaction. |
| `SetFont` | `void SetFont(Font font)` | Applies a font to the widget's text. Win32 sends `WM_SETFONT` with a cached `HFONT`; GTK overrides the widget's Pango font description. Native widgets use the platform tooltip rather than the toolkit's popup surface on purpose: a popup arms light dismiss and takes a pointer grab, which is right for a menu and quietly destructive for a tip, because the grab swallows the very clicks the user is aiming at the control underneath. The platform tip never takes input, and it is themed by the OS for free. |

Owner-drawn controls open their menu from the canvas mouse pipeline instead, so their peer never raises this. |

#### `IPopupPeer`

A light-dismiss floating surface: the native side of ComboBox drop-downs, menus, tooltips and calendar fly-outs. It is a full `ICanvasPeer`, so popup content is owner-drawn (and can even host native children) exactly like any other surface — a backend implements drawing and input once and the popup inherits it. Unlike a child canvas it floats above every window at a screen position, does not steal activation from its owner, and dismisses itself when the user clicks outside it, it loses the grab that routes that click to it, or Escape is pressed.

Implements `ICanvasPeer`, `IContainerPeer`, `IControlPeer`, `IDisposable`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LightDismiss` | `bool LightDismiss { get; set; }` | Whether showing the surface arms light dismiss — the pointer grab that routes the next click anywhere in the application to this surface so it can close itself. Defaults to `true`, which is what a menu, a drop-down list or a fly-out calendar wants: the click that closes them belongs to them. |
| `OutsidePointerMove` | `Action<Point> OutsidePointerMove { get; set; }` | Offered pointer motion that landed outside this surface, in screen coordinates. The grab that keeps a menu's deepest level catching outside clicks also redirects motion over shallower levels to it, so without this hook moving back onto a parent menu would neither re-highlight its rows nor open a sibling submenu — the hover would freeze the moment a submenu opened. A backend delivers this only when its grab reports out-of-surface motion (GTK); one whose capture reports motion to the surface's own canvas instead (Win32) leaves it unused, and a passive surface never sets it. |
| `OutsidePress` | `Func<Point, bool> OutsidePress { get; set; }` | Offered a press that landed outside this surface, in screen coordinates, before it light-dismisses. The owner returns `true` when it consumed the press — a menu whose deepest level holds the grab uses this to recognize a click on a shallower level of the same cascade and route it there rather than tearing the whole menu down. A false result, or no handler, dismisses as usual. Without it the grab that catches genuine outside clicks also swallows clicks on the parent menu. |
| `ExpectGrabHandoff` | `void ExpectGrabHandoff()` | Tells the surface that its light-dismiss grab is about to be handed off to a child popup it is opening, so the resulting grab loss is expected and must not dismiss it — consumed by the next grab loss. This is what lets a menu cascade open a submenu without the parent level closing. A surface that takes no grab (a tooltip) needs nothing here, hence the no-op default. |
| `Hide` | `void Hide()` | Hides the surface and releases any grab, without raising `Dismissed`. |
| `Regrab` | `void Regrab()` | Re-takes the light-dismiss grab a now-closed child popup held, so this surface again catches outside clicks and Escape. A no-op if it already holds the grab, is hidden, or never grabs. |
| `Resize` | `void Resize(Size size)` | Resizes an already-shown surface in place, leaving its position, its grab and its stacking alone. A filtered menu shrinks as it narrows, and re-showing it to do that would hand the grab round again mid-gesture — which is exactly the churn multi-level light dismiss is fragile to. A backend that cannot resize a mapped surface keeps the size it opened with, hence the no-op default. |
| `SetParentPopup` | `void SetParentPopup(IPopupPeer parent)` | Anchors this surface to another popup as its parent instead of the owning window — the relationship a submenu has to the menu level that opened it. On a stacked-popup display server (Wayland) a nested popup must chain to the top-most mapped popup, not the root window, or the server refuses to map it and the submenu never appears. Must be set before `ShowAt`. A backend whose popups are free-floating top-levels (Win32) needs nothing here, hence the no-op default. |
| `ShowAt` | `void ShowAt(Point screenLocation, Size size)` | Shows the surface at the given screen position with the given size, arming light dismiss unless `LightDismiss` was turned off. |
| `Dismissed` | `event EventHandler Dismissed` | Raised when the user dismisses the surface: a click outside it, loss of the activation/grab that keeps it up, or Escape. The surface is hidden first, then the event is raised. |

#### `BindingExtensions`

The lambda binding sugar over `PropertyBinding`: fluent, control-first overloads so a binding reads as one line at the call site — `label.Bind(vm, nameof(vm.Count), v => v.Display, (c, text) => c.Text = text)`. Strings appear only as the `nameof(...)` change-notification filter; member access is always a compiled delegate, so everything here survives trimming and NativeAOT.

| `Bind` | `static PropertyBinding<TValue> Bind<TControl, TSource, TValue>(this TControl target, TSource source, string sourcePropertyName, Func<TSource, TValue> getSource, Action<TControl, TValue> setTarget, Action<TSource, TValue> setSource, Func<TControl, TValue> getTarget, Action<TControl, EventHandler> subscribeTargetChanged, Action<TControl, EventHandler> unsubscribeTargetChanged, BindingMode mode = 1, BindingFallback<TValue> defaultValue = null, BindingFallback<TValue> nullReplacement = null, Action<string> onError = null)` | Binds a source property to this control with write-back: target edits, reported through the subscribed change event, flow into `setSource`. |

Supports `OneWay` and `OneTime`; the write-back modes need the full two-way overload. |

#### `BindingFallback<T>`

An optional per-binding fallback value — a tiny allocation-free "value or absent" wrapper that lets a binding tell a deliberately supplied `default(T)` apart from "no fallback given". Callers never construct it explicitly: passing a plain value to a `defaultValue`/ `nullReplacement`/`fallbackValue` parameter converts implicitly, and omitting the parameter means `None`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `IsSet` | `bool IsSet { get; }` | Whether a fallback value was supplied. |
| `None` | `static BindingFallback<T> None { get; }` | No fallback — the binding's default behavior applies. |
| `implicit operator BindingFallback<T>` | `static implicit operator BindingFallback<T>(T value)` | Wraps a value so plain arguments read naturally at the call site. |

#### `BindingMode`

How values flow across a `PropertyBinding`.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OneWay` | `0` | Source changes are pushed to the target; the target never writes back. |
| `TwoWay` | `1` | Changes flow both ways. |
| `OneWayToSource` | `2` | Target changes are written back to the source; the source never pushes. |
| `OneTime` | `3` | The source value is applied to the target once, at bind time, and never again. |

#### `ChainedBinding<TRoot, TMid, TValue>`

A one-way nested-path binding (`root.Mid.Value`) built from chained typed selectors — the reflection-free answer to `"a.b.c"` path strings. It observes the root for replacements of the middle object and the middle object for changes of the leaf value, re-subscribing whenever the middle link swaps and unsubscribing from the one it left behind. Deeper paths compose by nesting: let the change callback drive another chain.

Implements `IDisposable`.

A reflection-free binding between a source property (on an `INotifyPropertyChanged`) and an arbitrary target, expressed entirely through delegates. Because the accessors are compiled delegates rather than `PropertyDescriptor`/`TypeDescriptor` lookups, binding survives trimming and NativeAOT and costs nothing at steady state beyond the event subscription. This is the primitive the higher-level control data-binding layer is built on; it equally serves MVVM, MVC and MVP.

Implements `IDisposable`.

A `PropertyBinding` whose source and target hold different types, bridged by a delegate converter pair — the reflection-free `IValueConverter` equivalent. #### `AnimatedImage`

A decoded image — still or animated — ready to paint. It keeps the raw frame pixels and lazily realizes each frame's `IImage` against whatever backend paints it. Which frame shows is a pure function of elapsed time, not of a tick counter, so an animation stays in sync whether or not it has been on screen: a control that was hidden and comes back paints the exact frame it would have shown had it never been hidden (the elapsed time is taken modulo the loop).

Implements `IDisposable`, `IImage`.

| `IsAnimated` | `bool IsAnimated { get; }` | Whether there is more than one frame. |
| `LoopCount` | `int LoopCount { get; set; }` | How many times the animation plays before it stops on the last frame: 0 loops forever, 1 plays once (no loop), N plays N times. Defaults to the value the format declared. |
| `Width` | `int Width { get; }` | The pixel width, shared by every frame. |

Time is taken modulo one loop's duration, so the result is the same whether or not the image was on screen the whole time; once `LoopCount` loops have elapsed it stays on the final frame. |

#### `ITheme`

The palette, font and metrics an owner-drawn control uses so it matches the host desktop. Backends populate it from the OS (uxtheme/`GetSysColor` on Windows, `GtkStyleContext` on GTK, `NSColor` on macOS); `DefaultTheme` is the fallback for headless/test use. Painting exclusively through these members is what lets a custom control look native in light or dark mode. A theme is an immutable snapshot: after the desktop changes, the backend raises `ThemeChanged` and serves a fresh instance. Pixel metrics (`RowHeight`, `ScrollBarSize`) are logical: they are sized for the primary monitor's current scale, so painting them 1:1 there is correct; mapping onto another monitor's scale goes through `LogicalToDevice`.

#### `ImageDecoder`

A small pure-managed image decoder, so icons ship as ordinary `.png`/`.ico` bytes without dragging a native codec or an imaging library into the footprint (PRD §8). Deliberately a subset, honest about its edges: PNG — 8-bit-per-channel non-interlaced images in grayscale, grayscale+alpha, RGB, RGBA or palette form, all five scanline filters; the zlib stream is inflated with `DeflateStream` (header and Adler32 trailer skipped), and chunk CRCs are not verified — the input is the application's own embedded resource, not hostile data. `tRNS` palette transparency and 16-bit channels are not supported. ICO/CUR — directory parsing plus per-entry decoding of embedded PNGs and classic `BI_RGB` bitmaps: 32-bit BGRA (its own alpha channel) and 24-bit BGR with the 1-bit AND mask supplying transparency; a CUR is an ICO with directory type 2. BMP — uncompressed `BI_RGB` at 8-bit (palette), 24-bit and 32-bit, bottom-up or top-down. JPEG — baseline and progressive DCT at 8-bit precision, grayscale or three components, any sampling factors, restart intervals; arithmetic, lossless and CMYK files are rejected by name rather than approximated. See `ImageDecoder.Jpeg.cs`. PCX — RLE, 8-bit indexed (VGA trailer palette) or 24-bit (three 8-bit planes). GIF (87a/89a) — LZW image data composited onto the logical screen with per-frame delay, disposal and transparency, and the NETSCAPE loop count, producing a multi-frame `DecodedImage`. ANI (RIFF/ACON) — the `fram` list of ICO/CUR frames with the `anih` rate and optional `rate`/`seq` chunks, looping forever. The `Decode` entry point sniffs the format from the leading bytes and returns a `DecodedImage` (one frame for the stills, several for GIF/ANI).

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DecodeAni` | `static DecodedImage DecodeAni(ReadOnlySpan<byte> data)` | Decodes an ANI (RIFF/ACON) cursor animation: the `fram` list of ICO/CUR frames, the `anih` default rate, and the optional `rate`/`seq` chunks, into frames that loop forever. |
| `DecodeBmp` | `static ValueTuple<int, int, int[]> DecodeBmp(ReadOnlySpan<byte> data)` | Decodes an uncompressed (`BI_RGB`) BMP — 8-bit palette, 24-bit BGR or 32-bit BGRX, bottom-up or (negative height) top-down — into row-major 32-bit ARGB. |
| `DecodeCur` | `static ValueTuple<int, int, int[]> DecodeCur(ReadOnlySpan<byte> data, int preferredSize = 0)` | Decodes a CUR cursor container. Structurally an ICO with directory type 2 (its planes/bitcount fields carry the hotspot instead), so the image pixels decode the same way; the hotspot is not returned since the pixels are what a surface blits. |
| `DecodeCursor` | `static ValueTuple<int, int, int[], int, int> DecodeCursor(ReadOnlySpan<byte> data)` | Decodes bytes into a pointer image: an ICO/CUR (the CUR's hotspot comes back), an ANI (its first frame), or any still image (hotspot 0,0). The hotspot is the pixel the click aligns to. |
| `DecodeGif` | `static DecodedImage DecodeGif(ReadOnlySpan<byte> data)` | Decodes a GIF (87a/89a) — LZW image data, per-frame graphic control (delay, disposal, transparency) composited onto the logical screen, and the NETSCAPE loop count — into frames. |

#### `RtfSerializer`

Writes and reads the RTF subset NativeForms speaks: character styles (bold/italic/underline/ strikeout), text color, font size, paragraph alignment and bullets over plain text runs. The writer's output is plain standard RTF — WordPad and Word open it — and the reader is a tolerant subset parser: control words outside the subset are skipped, so it also digests the richer documents a native Win32 rich edit produces, keeping whatever falls inside the subset.
